title.raw: 卷五十七 列傳第三十八 魏虜 Volume 57 Biographies 38: Wei Prisoners

sentences.zh: 魏虜

translations.literal: The Wei Barbarians
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei

sentences.zh: 魏虜，匈奴種也，姓托跋氏。

translations.literal: The Wei barbarians were of Xiongnu stock and bore the surname Tuoba.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei were of Xiongnu descent and took the surname Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 晉，并州刺史劉琨為屠各胡劉聰所攻，索頭猗盧遣子曰利孫將兵救琨於太原，猗盧入居代郡，亦謂鮮卑。

translations.literal: In Jin times, Liu Kun, governor of Bing Province, was attacked by the Tugehu Liu Cong; Yilu of the Suotou sent his son Li-sun with troops to rescue Kun at Taiyuan; Yilu entered and settled in Dai Commandery—they were also called Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin, Liu Kun, governor of Bing Province, came under attack by the Tugehu chieftain Liu Cong. Yilu of the Suotou Xianbei sent his son Li-sun with an army to relieve Kun at Taiyuan, and Yilu then settled in Dai Commandery; they were also known as Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 被髮左衽，故呼為索頭。

translations.literal: With hair worn loose and coats folded to the left, they were therefore called Suotou.
translations.idiomatic: Because they wore their hair loose and folded their coats to the left, they were called Suotou—"Disheveled Heads."

sentences.zh: 猗盧孫什翼犍，字鬱律旃，後還陰山為單于，領匈奴諸部，

translations.literal: Yilu's grandson Shiyijian, styled Yulüzhan, later returned to Yinshan as Shanyu and ruled the Xiongnu tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu's grandson Shiyijian, courtesy name Yulüzhan, later withdrew to Yinshan as Shanyu and led the various Xiongnu tribes.

sentences.zh: 苻堅遣偽并州刺史苻洛伐犍，破龍庭，禽犍還長安，為立宅，教犍書學。

translations.literal: [In 371,] Fu Jian sent the false governor of Bing Fu Luo to attack Jian, broke Longting, captured Jian and took him back to Chang'an, built him a residence, and taught Jian writing and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent his puppet governor of Bing, Fu Luo, against Shiyijian, shattered Longting, seized him, and brought him to Chang'an, where he was given a house and instructed in letters and learning.

sentences.zh: 分其部黨君雲中等四郡，諸部主帥歲終入朝，并得見犍，差稅諸部以給之。

translations.literal: He divided their tribal followers into four commanderies including Yunzhong; the chiefs of the tribes came to court at year's end and all could see Jian; levies were assessed on the tribes to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were split among four commanderies, Yunzhong among them; tribal chiefs came to court each winter and were allowed to see Shiyijian, while levies from the tribes were assigned to maintain him.

sentences.zh: 堅敗，子珪，字涉圭，隨舅慕容垂據中山，還領其部，後稍彊盛，

translations.literal: After Jian was defeated, his son Gui, styled Shegui, followed his maternal uncle Murong Chui in holding Zhongshan, returned to lead his tribe, and gradually grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's fall, his son Gui, courtesy name Shegui, followed his uncle Murong Chui in occupying Zhongshan, resumed leadership of his people, and gradually grew powerful.

sentences.zh: 珪破慕容寶於中山，遂有并州，僭稱魏，年號天

translations.literal: [In 386,] Gui defeated Murong Bao at Zhongshan, then held Bing Province, usurped the title Wei, and took the era name Tian
translations.idiomatic: Gui defeated Murong Bao at Zhongshan, seized Bing Province, declared himself ruler of Wei, and adopted the reign title Tian

translations.literal: (auspicious omen)
translations.idiomatic: (auspicious omen)

translations.literal: [Gift].
translations.idiomatic: [Gift]—completing the era name Tianci, "Heaven's Gift."

sentences.zh: 追諡犍烈祖文平皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Jian as Emperor Liezu Wenping.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian was posthumously titled Emperor Liezu Wenping.

sentences.zh: 珪死，諡道武皇帝，子木末立，年號太常，死，諡明元皇帝。

translations.literal: When Gui died he was styled Emperor Daowu; his son Mumu succeeded with the era Taichang; when he died he was styled Emperor Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui died he received the temple name Emperor Daowu. His son Mumu succeeded under the era Taichang; at his death he was styled Emperor Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 子燾，字佛狸代立，年號太平真君。

translations.literal: His son Tao, styled Foli, succeeded in Dai with the era Taiping Zhenjun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao, courtesy name Foli, came to the throne and took the era Taiping Zhenjun.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，偽太子晃與大臣崔氏、寇氏不睦，崔、寇譖之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Song, the false crown prince Huang was on bad terms with the ministers of the Cui and Kou clans; Cui and Kou slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: During Song's Yuanjia reign, Crown Prince Huang fell out with ministers of the Cui and Kou families, who then slandered him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄高道人有道術，晃使祈福七日七夜，佛狸夢其祖父竝怒，手刃向之曰：「汝何故信讒，欲害太子！」

translations.literal: The Daoist Xuan Gao had occult arts; Huang had him pray for blessings seven days and seven nights; Foli dreamed that his grandfather Bing was furious, blade in hand advancing on him and saying, "Why do you believe slander and wish to harm the crown prince!"
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist master Xuan Gao possessed occult powers; Huang had him perform seven days and seven nights of prayer. Foli dreamed that his grandfather Bing stood before him in rage, blade raised, crying, "Why do you heed slander and seek to destroy the crown prince!"

sentences.zh: 佛狸驚覺，下偽詔曰：「王者大業，纂承為重，儲宮嗣紹，百王舊例。

translations.literal: Foli awoke in alarm and issued a false edict saying, "The great enterprise of kings weighs most heavily on succession; the heir apparent continuing the line is the ancient rule of the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Startled awake, Foli issued an edict: "A king's great enterprise rests above all on succession; investiture of the heir is the immemorial custom of the hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 自今已往，事無巨細，必經太子，然後上聞。」

translations.literal: From this time forward, matters great and small must pass through the crown prince before being reported above."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whether the matter be great or small, it must go through the crown prince before reaching me."

sentences.zh: 晃後謀殺佛狸見殺。

translations.literal: Later Huang plotted to kill Foli and was himself killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huang plotted to assassinate Foli and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 燾死，諡太武皇帝。

translations.literal: When Tao died he was styled Emperor Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao died he received the temple name Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 立晃子濬，字烏雷直勤，年號和平。

translations.literal: Huang's son Jun was installed, styled Wulei Zhiqin, with the era Heping.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's son Jun succeeded, courtesy name Wulei Zhiqin, under the era Heping.

sentences.zh: 追諡晃景穆皇帝。

translations.literal: Huang was posthumously styled Emperor Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was posthumously titled Emperor Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 濬死，諡文成皇帝。

translations.literal: When Jun died he was styled Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun died he was styled Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 子弘字萬民立，年號天安，

translations.literal: His son Hong, styled Wanmin, succeeded with the era Tian'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, courtesy name Wanmin, came to the throne under the era Tian'an.

sentences.zh: 偽太子宏生，改年為皇興。

translations.literal: [In 467,] the false crown prince Hong was born; the era was changed to Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Hong was born, the reign was renamed Huangxing.

sentences.zh: 什翼珪始都平城，猶逐水草，無城郭，木末始土著居處。

translations.literal: Shiyijian first made Pingcheng the capital but still followed water and grass, without walls or cities; Mumu was the first to settle in fixed dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiyijian first established his capital at Pingcheng, the people still followed pasture and water and had no walled towns; only under Mumu did they begin to live in settled habitations.

sentences.zh: 佛狸破梁州、黃龍，徙其居民，大築郭邑。

translations.literal: Foli conquered Liang Province and Huanglong, moved their inhabitants, and greatly built outer cities.
translations.idiomatic: Foli conquered Liangzhou and Huanglong, relocated the inhabitants, and undertook large-scale construction of walled districts.

sentences.zh: 截平城西為宮城，四角起樓，女墻，門不施屋，城又無壍。

translations.literal: He cut off the western part of Pingcheng as the palace city, raised towers at the four corners with battlements; the gates had no roof structures, and the city had no moat.
translations.idiomatic: The western section of Pingcheng was taken as the palace precinct, with towers at each corner and crenellated parapets; the gates had no gatehouses, and there was no moat.

sentences.zh: 南門外立二土門，內立廟，開四門，各隨方色，凡五廟，一世一閒，瓦屋。

translations.literal: Outside the south gate two earthen gates were set up; within, temples were built with four gates, each in the color of its direction; five temples in all, one chamber per generation, with tiled roofs.
translations.idiomatic: Two earthen gates stood outside the south gate; inside were ancestral temples with four gates painted according to the colors of the four directions—five temples in all, one hall per reign, roofed with tile.

sentences.zh: 其西立太社。

translations.literal: To the west the Grand Altar of Soil was established.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood the Grand Altar of Soil.

sentences.zh: 佛狸所居雲母等三殿，又立重屋，居其上。

translations.literal: The three halls where Foli dwelled, including the Mica Hall, had upper stories built, and he lived above.
translations.idiomatic: Foli's residence included three halls such as the Mica Hall; upper stories were added, and he lived on the top floor.

sentences.zh: 飲食廚名「阿真廚」，在西，皇后可孫恒出此廚求食。

translations.literal: The food kitchen was called the "Azhen Kitchen," in the west; the empress Kesun always went to this kitchen to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: The dining kitchen was called the "Azhen Kitchen" and lay to the west; Empress Kesun regularly went there herself for meals.

sentences.zh: 初，姚興以塞外虜赫連勃勃為安北將軍，領五部胡，屯大城，姚泓敗後，入長安。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao Xing had made the frontier barbarian Helian Bobo Pacifier of the North and general, leading the Five-Department Hu, stationed at Dacheng; after Yao Hong was defeated, he entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yao Xing had appointed the frontier chieftain Helian Bobo Pacifier of the North, with command over the Five-Department Hu, garrisoned at Dacheng; after Yao Hong's defeat he entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 佛狸攻破勃勃子昌，娶勃勃女為皇后。

translations.literal: Foli attacked and defeated Bobo's son Chang and took Bobo's daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Foli defeated Bobo's son Chang and married Bobo's daughter as his empress.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，仇池公楊盛表云「索虜勃勃，匈奴正胤」是也。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era, Duke Yang Sheng of Chouchi memorialized saying, "The Suotou barbarian Bobo is the true heir of the Xiongnu"—this is the reference.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yixi era, Duke Yang Sheng of Chouchi wrote in a memorial that "the Suotou chieftain Bobo is the legitimate Xiongnu line"—meaning this connection.

sentences.zh: 可孫昔妾媵之。

translations.literal: Kesun had once been a concubine attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kesun had once served among the concubine attendants.

sentences.zh: 殿西鎧仗庫屋四十餘閒，殿北絲綿布絹庫土屋一十餘閒。

translations.literal: West of the hall were more than forty chambers of the armor and weapons storehouse; north of the hall were more than ten earthen chambers of the silk, cotton, cloth, and silk-brocade storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: West of the hall stood more than forty rooms of the armory; north of the hall, more than ten earthen storehouses for silk, cotton, cloth, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 偽太子宮在城東，亦開四門，瓦屋，四角起樓。

translations.literal: The false crown prince's palace was east of the city, also with four gates, tiled roofs, and towers at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's palace lay east of the city, likewise with four gates, tiled roofs, and corner towers.

sentences.zh: 妃妾住皆土屋。

translations.literal: The consorts and concubines all lived in earthen houses.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and concubines all dwelled in earthen houses.

sentences.zh: 婢使千餘人，織綾錦販賣，酤酒，養猪羊，牧牛馬，種菜逐利。

translations.literal: More than a thousand servant women wove damask and brocade for sale, sold wine, raised pigs and sheep, herded cattle and horses, and planted vegetables for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand maidservants wove damask and brocade for market, sold wine, kept pigs and sheep, tended cattle and horses, and grew vegetables for profit.

sentences.zh: 太官八十餘窖，窖四千斛，半穀半米。

translations.literal: The imperial kitchen had more than eighty cellars, each cellar four thousand hu, half grain and half rice.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial kitchen maintained more than eighty granaries, each holding four thousand hu—half grain, half rice.

sentences.zh: 又有懸食瓦屋數十閒，置尚方作鐵及木。

translations.literal: There were also several tens of tiled chambers for hanging food, and the Imperial Workshop was set up for iron and wood work.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen tiled rooms held suspended provisions; the Imperial Workshop produced iron and woodwork.

sentences.zh: 其袍衣，使宮內婢為〔之〕。

translations.literal: Their robes and garments were made by palace servant women.
translations.idiomatic: Robes and garments were made by women of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 偽太子別有倉庫。

translations.literal: The false crown prince had separate storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince maintained separate storehouses of his own.

sentences.zh: 其郭城繞宮城南，悉築為坊，坊開巷。

translations.literal: The outer city wrapped around the south of the palace city; all was built into wards, and the wards opened onto lanes.
translations.idiomatic: The outer city ringed the palace to the south, entirely laid out in wards with lanes opening between them.

sentences.zh: 坊大者容四五百家，小者六七十家。

translations.literal: Large wards held four or five hundred households; small ones sixty or seventy.
translations.idiomatic: The largest wards held four or five hundred households; the smallest, sixty or seventy.

sentences.zh: 每南坊搜檢，以備奸巧。

translations.literal: Each southern ward was searched to guard against treachery and trickery.
translations.idiomatic: Southern wards were searched regularly to guard against subversion and fraud.

sentences.zh: 城西南去白登山七里，於山邊別立父祖廟。

translations.literal: Seven li southwest of the city was Mount Baideng; at the foot of the mountain ancestral temples to the fathers were separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Seven li southwest of the city stood Mount Baideng, where separate ancestral shrines to the forefathers were built at the mountain's foot.

sentences.zh: 城西有祠天壇，立四十九木人，長丈許，白幘、練裙、馬尾被，立壇上，常以四月四日殺牛馬祭祀，盛陳鹵簿，邊壇奔馳奏伎為樂。

translations.literal: West of the city was an altar for sacrificing to Heaven; forty-nine wooden figures about a zhang tall, with white headcloths, white silk skirts, and horse-tail cloaks, stood on the altar; on the fourth day of the fourth month cattle and horses were slaughtered in sacrifice, guards of honor were fully displayed, and around the altar riders galloped performing music and acrobatics for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: West of the city stood a Heaven altar with forty-nine wooden figures some ten feet tall, wearing white headcloths, white skirts, and horsehair cloaks. On the fourth day of the fourth month cattle and horses were sacrificed; the full guard of honor was displayed, and riders circled the altar at a gallop, performing music and acrobatics.

sentences.zh: 城西三里，刻石寫五經及其國記，於鄴取石虎文石屋基六十枚，皆長丈餘，以充用。

translations.literal: Three li west of the city, stones were carved with the Five Classics and their national chronicle; from Ye sixty foundation stones of Shi Hu's carved stone chambers were taken, each more than a zhang long, to serve the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Three li west of the city, stone stelae were inscribed with the Five Classics and the Wei state chronicle; sixty foundation blocks from Shi Hu's carved stone halls at Ye, each over ten feet long, were brought for the work.

sentences.zh: 國中呼內左右為「直真」，外左右為「烏矮真」，曹局文書吏為「比德真」，檐衣人為「樸大真」，帶仗人為「胡洛真」，通事人為「乞萬真」，守門人為「可薄真」，偽臺乘驛賤人為「拂竹真」，諸州乘驛人為「咸真」，殺人者為「契害真」，為主出受辭人為「折潰真」，貴人作食人為「附真」。

translations.literal: In the state the inner attendants were called "Zhizhen," the outer attendants "Wu'aizhen," clerks of bureau documents "Bidezhen," garment-bearers "Pudazhen," weapon-bearers "Huluozhen," interpreters "Qiwanzhen," gatekeepers "Kebozhen," the false court's lowly post-riders "Fuzhuzhen," post-riders of the provinces "Xianzhen," executioners "Qihaizhen," those who went out to receive testimony for the lord "Zhekuizhen," and cooks for nobles "Fuzhen."
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm the inner attendants were called zhizhen, the outer wu'aizhen; bureau clerks bidezhen; robe-bearers pudazhen; arms-bearers huluozhen; interpreters qiwanzhen; gatekeepers kebozhen; the court's humble courier-runners fuzhuzhen; provincial couriers xianzhen; executioners qihaizhen; agents who took testimony abroad zhekuizhen; and noble cooks fuzhen.

sentences.zh: 三公貴人，通謂之「羊真」。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes and nobles were generally called "Yangzhen."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies and great nobles were collectively termed yangzhen.

sentences.zh: 佛狸置三公、太宰、尚書令、僕射、侍中，與太子共決國事。

translations.literal: Foli appointed the Three Dukes, Grand Steward, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Director, and Attendant-in-Ordinary, who with the crown prince jointly decided state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Foli appointed the Three Excellencies, Grand Steward, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Director, and Attendants-in-Ordinary, who deliberated on state affairs together with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書知殿內兵馬倉庫，樂部尚書知伎樂及角史伍伯，駕部尚書知牛馬驢騾，南部尚書知南邊州郡，北部尚書知北邊州郡。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace supervised troops, horses, and storehouses within the palace; the Director of the Music Bureau supervised performers and musicians, horn clerks, and guards; the Director of the Chariot Bureau supervised cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules; the Southern Director supervised southern border provinces and commanderies; the Northern Director supervised northern border provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Director oversaw troops, horses, and stores within the palace; the Music Director, performers, musicians, and guard detachments; the Chariot Director, cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules; the Southern Director, southern frontier provinces; and the Northern Director, northern frontier provinces.

sentences.zh: 又有俟懃地何，比尚書；

translations.literal: There were also Qinhun Dihe, equivalent to Director;
translations.idiomatic: There was also the office of qinhun dihe, comparable to Director;

sentences.zh: 莫堤，比刺史；

translations.literal: Moti, equivalent to Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: moti, comparable to provincial inspector;

sentences.zh: 郁若，比二千石；

translations.literal: Yuruo, equivalent to two-thousand-dan rank;
translations.idiomatic: yuruo, comparable to the two-thousand-dan grade;

sentences.zh: 受別官比諸侯。

translations.literal: Shoubieguan was equivalent to feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: and shoubieguan, comparable to feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 諸曹府有倉庫，悉置比官，皆使通虜漢語，以為傳驛。

translations.literal: The various bureau offices had storehouses and all had equivalent officials; all were made to know both barbarian and Chinese speech for relay and transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau maintained storehouses and parallel offices; incumbents were required to know both Xianbei and Chinese for relay work.

sentences.zh: 蘭臺置中丞御史，知城內事。

translations.literal: The Orchid Terrace had Censor and Imperial Secretary to oversee matters within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Orchid Terrace housed censors who oversaw affairs within the capital.

sentences.zh: 又置九豆和官，宮城三里內民戶籍不屬諸軍戍者，悉屬之。

translations.literal: The Jiudouhe office was also established; civilian households within three li of the palace city whose registers did not belong to military garrisons all fell under it.
translations.idiomatic: A jiudouhe office was also established; all civilian households within three li of the palace whose registers were not attached to garrisons came under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 其車服，有大小輦，皆五層，下施四輪，三二百人牽之，四施絙索，備傾倒。

translations.literal: Their carriages and regalia included large and small imperial carriages, all of five tiers, with four wheels below; two or three hundred men pulled them, and ropes were attached on four sides against overturning.
translations.idiomatic: Their carriages included great and small imperial litters, each of five tiers mounted on four wheels and drawn by two or three hundred men, with ropes rigged on all four sides against tipping.

sentences.zh: 軺車建龍旂，尚黑。

translations.literal: Light carriages bore dragon banners; black was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Light carriages flew dragon banners; black was the preferred color.

sentences.zh: 妃后則施雜綵幰，無幢絡。

translations.literal: Consorts and empresses used mixed-color canopies without pennant tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and empresses rode under multicolored canopies without pennant streamers.

sentences.zh: 太后出，則婦女著鎧騎馬近輦左右。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager went out, women in armor rode horses close to the left and right of the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager went abroad, armored women on horseback flanked the litter.

sentences.zh: 虜主及后妃常行，乘銀鏤羊車，不施帷幔，皆偏坐垂腳轅中；

translations.literal: The barbarian lord and consorts on ordinary outings rode silver-inlaid sheep carts without curtains, all sitting sideways with legs hanging in the shaft;
translations.idiomatic: On ordinary outings the Wei ruler and his consorts rode silver-inlaid sheep carts without curtains, sitting sideways with their legs dangling over the shafts;

sentences.zh: 在殿上，亦跂據。

translations.literal: in the hall they also sat with legs drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: in the hall they likewise sat with legs drawn up beneath them.

sentences.zh: 正殿施流蘇帳，金博山，龍鳳朱漆畫屏風，織成幌。

translations.literal: The main hall had tasseled curtains, a golden Boshan censer, dragon-and-phoenix screens painted in red lacquer, and woven curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall was hung with tasseled curtains, a golden Boshan incense mountain, red-lacquered dragon-and-phoenix screens, and woven valances.

sentences.zh: 坐施氍毹褥。

translations.literal: For seating, wool rugs and cushions were spread.
translations.idiomatic: Wool rugs and cushions were spread for seating.

sentences.zh: 前施金香鑪，琉璃鉢，金椀，盛雜食器。

translations.literal: Before them were set golden incense burners, glass bowls, golden bowls, and vessels holding assorted foods.
translations.idiomatic: Before them stood golden censers, glass bowls, gold dishes, and vessels for assorted foods.

sentences.zh: 設客長盤一尺，御饌圓盤廣一丈。

translations.literal: Guests' long trays were a chi; the imperial round tray for food was ten chi across.
translations.idiomatic: Guests were served on long trays a foot wide; the imperial banquet was laid on a round platter ten feet across.

sentences.zh: 為四輪車，元會日，六七十人牽上殿。

translations.literal: It was made a four-wheeled cart; on New Year's day sixty or seventy men pulled it up into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The platter was mounted on a four-wheeled cart; on New Year's day sixty or seventy men hauled it into the hall.

sentences.zh: 蜡日逐除，歲盡，城門磔雄雞，葦索桃梗，如漢儀。

translations.literal: On the La festival day they drove out the old; at year's end at the city gates a cock was dismembered, with reed ropes and peach staffs, as in Han ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the La festival they performed the year-end expulsion; at the city gates a rooster was sacrificed and reed ropes with peach staffs set up, following Han custom.

sentences.zh: 自佛狸至萬民，世增雕飾。

translations.literal: From Foli to Wanmin, each generation added ornament and carving.
translations.idiomatic: From Foli's reign through Wanmin's, each generation added further ornament.

sentences.zh: 正殿西築土臺，謂之白樓。

translations.literal: West of the main hall an earthen terrace was built, called the White Tower.
translations.idiomatic: West of the main hall rose an earthen terrace called the White Tower.

sentences.zh: 萬民禪位後，常遊觀其上。

translations.literal: After Wanmin abdicated he often strolled and viewed from atop it.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanmin abdicated he often strolled there to take in the view.

sentences.zh: 臺南又有伺星樓。

translations.literal: South of the terrace was also a Star-Watching Tower.
translations.idiomatic: South of the terrace stood a Star-Watching Tower.

sentences.zh: 正殿西又有祠屋，琉璃為瓦。

translations.literal: West of the main hall were also shrine buildings with glazed tiles.
translations.idiomatic: West of the main hall were shrine halls roofed with glazed tiles.

sentences.zh: 宮門稍覆以屋，猶不知為重樓。

translations.literal: Palace gates were slightly roofed over, but they still did not understand multi-storied buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gates were given modest roof coverings, but they had not yet adopted true multi-storied gate towers.

sentences.zh: 竝設削泥采，畫金剛力士。

translations.literal: Colored plaster relief was also set up, painting vajra guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Colored plaster reliefs were installed, depicting vajra guardian figures.

sentences.zh: 胡俗尚水，又規畫黑龍相盤繞，以為厭勝，

translations.literal: Barbarian custom esteemed water; black dragons coiling around each other were also drawn as apotropaic symbols.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian custom favored water symbolism; coiling black dragons were painted as charms against evil.

sentences.zh: 萬民禪位子宏，自稱太上皇。

translations.literal: [In 471,] Wanmin abdicated the throne to his son Hong and styled himself Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wanmin abdicated in favor of his son Hong and took the title Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 宏立，號。

translations.literal: Hong succeeded; his title [era name follows].
translations.idiomatic: Hong came to the throne; his reign title [follows in the next line].

sentences.zh: 至六年，萬民死，諡獻文皇帝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Wanmin died and was styled Emperor Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of his reign Wanmin died and was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 改號為承明元年，是歲也。

translations.literal: The era was changed to the first year of Chengming—that was this year.
translations.idiomatic: The era was changed to Chengming year one—the year of his death.

sentences.zh: 祖母馮氏，黃龍人，助治國事。

translations.literal: The grandmother, Lady Feng, a native of Huanglong, assisted in governing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother, Lady Feng of Huanglong, helped administer state affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，佛狸母是漢人，為木末所殺，佛狸以乳母為太后，自此以來，太子立，輒誅其母。

translations.literal: Earlier, Foli's mother was a Han woman and was killed by Mumu; Foli made his wet nurse empress dowager. From this time on, whenever a crown prince was installed, his mother was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Foli's birth mother had been Han and was killed by Mumu; Foli raised his wet nurse to empress dowager. Thereafter, whenever a crown prince was enthroned, his mother was executed.

sentences.zh: 一云馮氏本江都人，佛狸南侵，略得馮氏，濬以為妾，獨得全焉。

translations.literal: One account says the Feng clan were originally from Jiangdu; when Foli invaded south he captured Lady Feng; Jun took her as a concubine, and she alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Another account holds that the Fengs were originally from Jiangdu; Foli seized Lady Feng on a southern campaign, and Jun took her as a concubine—she alone escaped the customary fate.

sentences.zh: 明年丁巳歲，改號太和。

translations.literal: The next year, a dingsi year, the era was changed to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, a dingsi year, the reign was renamed Taihe.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝末年，始與虜和好。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Ming of Song, peace with the barbarians was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Ming of Song, peace was first made with the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 元徽昇明之世，虜使歲通，

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui and Shengming eras, barbarian envoys came every year.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhui and Shengming reigns, Wei envoys arrived annually.

sentences.zh: 偽太和三年也。

translations.literal: [This was] the third year of the false era Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: This was the third year of the Wei era Taihe.

sentences.zh: 宏聞太祖受禪，其冬，發眾遣丹陽王劉昶為太師，寇司、豫二州。

translations.literal: When Hong heard that the Founding Emperor had received the abdication, that winter he raised troops and sent Prince Liu Chang of Danyang as Grand Preceptor to invade Si and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong learned that the Founding Emperor of Qi had taken the throne, that winter he mobilized an army and sent Prince Liu Chang of Danyang as Grand Preceptor to raid Si and Yu provinces.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔遣眾軍北討。

translations.literal: The next year an edict dispatched the armies on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an imperial edict ordered a general northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 宏遣大將郁豆眷、叚長命攻壽陽及鍾離，為豫州刺史垣崇祖、右將軍周盤龍、徐州刺史崔文仲等所破。

translations.literal: Hong sent the generals Yudoujuan and Duan Changming to attack Shouyang and Zhongli; they were defeated by Yuan Chongzu, governor of Yu Province, Right General Zhou Panlong, Cui Wenzong, governor of Xu Province, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent the generals Yudoujuan and Duan Changming against Shouyang and Zhongli, but they were routed by Yuan Chongzu, governor of Yu, Right General Zhou Panlong, Cui Wenzong, governor of Xu, and their colleagues.

sentences.zh: 宏又遣偽南部尚書托跋等向司州，分兵出兖、青界，十萬眾圍朐山，戍主玄元度嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Hong again sent the false Southern Director Tuoba and others toward Si Province; detachments issued from Yan and Qing borders; a hundred thousand men besieged Qushan; the garrison commander Xuan Yuandu closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Hong again sent the Southern Director Tuoba and others toward Si Province while detachments crossed from Yan and Qing; a hundred thousand troops besieged Qushan, whose commander Xuan Yuandu shut the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 青冀二州刺史盧紹之遣子奐領兵助之。

translations.literal: Lu Shaozhi, governor of Qing and Ji provinces, sent his son Huan with troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shaozhi, governor of Qing and Ji, sent his son Huan with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 城中無食，紹之出頓州南石頭亭，隔海運糧柴供給城內。

translations.literal: Within the city there was no food; Shaozhi went out and encamped at Shitou Pavilion south of the province, shipping grain and firewood across the sea to supply the city.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran short inside the city, Shaozhi withdrew to Shitou Pavilion south of the provincial seat and shipped grain and fuel across the sea to sustain the garrison.

sentences.zh: 虜圍斷海道，緣岸攻城，會潮水大至，虜渰溺，元度出兵奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The barbarians cut the sea route and attacked along the shore; just then the tide rose greatly and the barbarians were drowned; Yuandu sallied forth and struck fiercely, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei forces severed the sea lanes and pressed the assault along the shore, but a great tide swept in and drowned many; Yuandu sallied out and struck hard, inflicting a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 臺遣軍主崔靈建、楊法持、房靈民萬餘人從淮入海，船艦至夜各舉兩火，虜眾望見，謂是南軍大至，一時奔退。

translations.literal: The court sent the commanders Cui Lingjian, Yang Fachi, and Fang Lingmin with more than ten thousand men from the Huai into the sea; the ships at night each raised two fires; the barbarian host saw them and thought the southern army had arrived in force, and all at once fled.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched commanders Cui Lingjian, Yang Fachi, and Fang Lingmin with over ten thousand men from the Huai down to the sea; at night each ship raised two signal fires. The Wei troops, seeing them, believed a great southern fleet had arrived and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 初，元度自云臂上有封侯志，宋世以示世祖，時世祖在東宮，書與元度曰：「努力成臂上之相也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuandu himself said that on his arm was the mark of one destined for enfeoffment; in Song times he showed it to the Founding Emperor; at that time the Founding Emperor was in the Eastern Palace and wrote to Yuandu saying, "Strive to fulfill the sign on your arm."
translations.idiomatic: Yuandu had long claimed a birthmark on his arm foretelling ennoblement; during Song he showed it to the future Founding Emperor, then crown prince, who wrote back: "Strive to make good on that mark upon your arm."

sentences.zh: 虜退，上議加封爵，元度歸功於紹之，紹之又讓，故竝見寢。

translations.literal: After the barbarians withdrew, the court discussed adding enfeoffments and ranks; Yuandu attributed the merit to Shaozhi, and Shaozhi in turn declined, so both proposals were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army withdrew, the court debated rewards of rank; Yuandu credited Shaozhi, and Shaozhi declined in turn, so both ennoblements were set aside.

sentences.zh: 上乃擢紹之為黃門郎。

translations.literal: The emperor then promoted Shaozhi to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instead promoted Shaozhi to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 鬱州呼石頭亭為平虜亭。

translations.literal: Yuzhou called Shitou Pavilion the Pacify-Barbarians Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou renamed Shitou Pavilion the Pacify-Barbarians Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 紹之字子緒，范陽人，自云盧諶玄孫。

translations.literal: Shaozhi, styled Zixu, was a native of Fanyang and claimed to be the great-great-grandson of Lu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi, courtesy name Zixu, came from Fanyang and claimed descent from Lu Chen in the fourth generation.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，預攻廣陵，勳上，紹之拔迹自投，上以為州治中，受心腹之任。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song, during the attack on Guangling, when merit rolls were submitted, Shaozhi came forward of his own accord; the emperor made him provincial administrator and entrusted him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: During Song's Daming reign, in the campaign against Guangling, when merit rolls were submitted Shaozhi stepped forward on his own; the emperor appointed him provincial administrator and treated him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 官至光祿大夫，

translations.literal: He reached the office of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: [Later] he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 三年，領軍將軍李安民、左軍將軍孫文顯與虜軍戰於淮陽，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the third year, General of the Guards Li Anmin and Left General Sun Wenxian fought the barbarian army at Huaiyang and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, General of the Guards Li Anmin and Left General Sun Wenxian met the Wei army at Huaiyang and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 初，虜寇至，緣淮驅略，江北居民猶懲佛狸時事，皆驚走，不可禁止。

translations.literal: When the barbarians first raided, they drove and plundered along the Huai; residents north of the river, still mindful of Foli's time, all fled in panic and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei first invaded, they ravaged the Huai line; north-bank inhabitants, still remembering Foli's campaigns, fled in panic beyond all restraint.

sentences.zh: 乃於梁山置二軍，南置三軍，慈姥置一軍，洌州置二軍，三山置二軍，白沙洲置一軍，蔡州置五軍，長蘆置三軍，菰浦置二軍，徐浦置一軍，內外悉班階賞，以示威刑。

translations.literal: Then two armies were posted at Liangshan, three armies to the south, one at Cilao, two at Liezhou, two at Sanshan, one at Baishazhou, five at Caizhou, three at Changlu, two at Gupu, one at Xupu; inside and outside, ranks and rewards were all distributed to display authority and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court posted two armies at Liangshan, three to the south, one at Cilao, two at Liezhou, two at Sanshan, one at Baishazhou, five at Caizhou, three at Changlu, two at Gupu, and one at Xupu, distributing ranks and rewards throughout the command to display both favor and severity.

sentences.zh: 偽昌黎王馮莎向司州，荒人桓天生說莎云：「諸蠻皆響應。」

translations.literal: The false Prince of Changli Feng Sha advanced toward Si Province; the frontier man Huan Tiansheng told Sha, "All the Man tribes will respond."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changli Feng Sha marched on Si Province; the frontier leader Huan Tiansheng assured him that "all the southern tribes will rise in answer."

sentences.zh: 莎至，蠻竟不動。

translations.literal: When Sha arrived, the Man in the end did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: When Sha arrived, the tribes never stirred.

sentences.zh: 莎大怒，於淮邊獵而去。

translations.literal: Sha was greatly angered and withdrew after hunting along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Sha hunted along the Huai and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及壽春摧敗，朐山不拔，虜主出定州，大治道路，聲欲南行，不敢進。

translations.literal: When Shouyang was crushed in defeat and Qushan could not be taken, the barbarian lord went out to Ding Province and greatly repaired the roads, proclaiming that he would march south but not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat at Shouyang and failure at Qushan, the Wei ruler moved to Ding Province and repaired the roads on a grand scale, proclaiming a southern march but daring not advance.

sentences.zh: 迺與偽梁郡王計曰：「兵出彭、泗間，無復鬬志，要當一兩戰得還歸。」

translations.literal: He then plotted with the false Prince of Liang Commandery, saying, "When the army came out between Peng and Si, there was no more will to fight; we need only one or two battles to get home."
translations.idiomatic: He confided to the Prince of Liang Commandery: "Once our men were between the Peng and Si, they lost heart; we need only a battle or two before we can turn home."

sentences.zh: 既於淮陽被破，一時奔走。

translations.literal: After being defeated at Huaiyang, they fled all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at Huaiyang, they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 青、徐間赴義民，先是或抄虜運車，更相殺掠，往往得南歸者數千家。

translations.literal: Righteous volunteers between Qing and Xu had earlier sometimes raided barbarian supply wagons and killed and plundered one another; often several thousand households were able to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteer bands in Qing and Xu had earlier ambushed Wei supply trains and sometimes preyed on one another, yet thousands of households often made their way back south.

sentences.zh: 上未遑外略，以虜既摧破，且欲示以威懷，遣後軍參軍車僧朗北使。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet turned to external campaigns; since the barbarians were already broken, and wishing also to display both might and conciliation, he sent Rear Army Adjutant Che Senglang as envoy north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, not yet ready for further campaigns abroad, sent Rear Army Adjutant Che Senglang north as envoy—both because the Wei were already broken and because he wished to show strength joined to conciliation.

sentences.zh: 虜問僧朗曰：「齊輔宋日淺，何故便登天位？」

translations.literal: The barbarians asked Senglang, "Qi aided Song only a short time—why then ascend the throne so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei asked Senglang: "Qi has assisted Song only briefly—why seize the throne so soon?"

sentences.zh: 僧朗曰：「虞、夏登庸，親當革禪；

translations.literal: Senglang said, "Yu and Xia took the throne by elevation and personally carried out the change of mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Senglang replied: "Yu and Xia took power by elevation and personally performed the transfer of the mandate;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉匡

translations.literal: Wei and Jin assisted
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin assisted

translations.literal: (battle)
translations.idiomatic: (battle)

sentences.zh: 〔輔〕，貽厥子孫。

translations.literal: [supported], bequeathing to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: [the throne], bequeathing it to their descendants.

sentences.zh: 豈二聖促促於天位，兩賢謙虛以獨善？

translations.literal: How could the two sages be hasty about the heavenly throne, or the two worthies modestly seek private good alone?
translations.idiomatic: Were those two sage rulers to hurry onto the throne, or those two worthy ministers to retire into private virtue alone?

sentences.zh: 時宜各異，豈得一揆？

translations.literal: The times and their fitness differ—how could there be one measure?
translations.idiomatic: Times differ in what they require—how could one rule fit all?

sentences.zh: 苟曰事宜，故屈己應物。」

translations.literal: If it is said to suit the times, then one bends oneself to respond to circumstances."
translations.idiomatic: When the times demand it, one bends oneself to answer circumstance."

sentences.zh: 虜又問：「齊主悉有何功業？」

translations.literal: The barbarians asked again, "What achievements does the lord of Qi have?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again: "What deeds has the lord of Qi to his credit?"

sentences.zh: 僧朗曰：「主上聖性寬仁，天識弘遠。

translations.literal: Senglang said, "Our lord is sage in nature, broad and humane, with heaven-granted insight far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Senglang answered: "Our lord is sage and humane by nature, with vision granted from heaven.

sentences.zh: 少為宋文皇所器遇，入參禁旅。

translations.literal: In youth he was valued by Emperor Wen of Song and entered service in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Emperor Wen of Song singled him out for favor and brought him into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 泰始之初，四方寇叛，東平劉子房、張淹，北討薛索兒，兼掌軍國，豫司顧命。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, rebels rose on all sides; he pacified Liu Zifang and Zhang Yan in the east, campaigned north against Xue Suo'er, held both military and civil power, and received the dying charge for Yu and Si.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi, rebellion broke out everywhere; he pacified Liu Zifang and Zhang Yan in the east, campaigned north against Xue Suo'er, held joint civil and military authority, and received the regent's charge for Yu and Si provinces.

sentences.zh: 宋桂陽、建平二王阻兵內侮，一麾殄滅。

translations.literal: The two princes of Guiyang and Jianping of Song raised armies and made internal war; with one command he exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Guiyang and Jianping raised armies in civil war; he destroyed them at a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王反道敗德，有過桀、紂，遠遵伊、霍，行廢立之事。

translations.literal: Prince Cangwu violated the Way and ruined virtue, exceeding Jie and Zhou; following Yi and Huo from afar, he carried out deposition and installation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cangwu violated the Way and outdid Jie and Zhou in wickedness; following the example of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, our lord deposed and enthroned rulers.

sentences.zh: 袁粲、劉秉、沈攸之同惡相濟，又秉旄杖鉞，大定凶黨。

translations.literal: Yuan Can, Liu Bing, and Shen Youzhi aided one another in evil; again bearing banners and battle-axes, he greatly settled the wicked faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can, Liu Bing, and Shen Youzhi joined in rebellion, he took up banner and axe and crushed the traitor faction.

sentences.zh: 戮力佐時，四十餘載，經綸夷險，十五六年，此功此德，可謂物無異議。」

translations.literal: Exerting strength to assist the age for more than forty years, ordering affairs through peace and peril for fifteen or sixteen years—such merit and such virtue may be said to leave no dissent among men."
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years he labored to sustain the age, and for fifteen or sixteen he steered the state through calm and crisis—merit and virtue on which none can disagree."

sentences.zh: 虜又問：「南國無復齊土，何故封齊？」

translations.literal: The barbarians asked again, "The southern state no longer has Qi territory—why enfeoff as Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: They pressed again: "The south no longer holds Qi lands—why take the title Qi?"

sentences.zh: 僧朗曰：「營丘表海，實為大國。

translations.literal: Senglang said, "Yingqiu faces the sea and is truly a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Senglang replied: "Yingqiu faces the sea—it was always a great state.

sentences.zh: 宋朝光啟土宇，謂是呂尚先封。

translations.literal: The Song dynasty expanded its territory and took this to be the original enfeoffment of Lü Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The Song dynasty, expanding its realm, held this to be the original fief of Lü Shang.

sentences.zh: 今淮海之間，自有青、齊，非無地也。」

translations.literal: Now between the Huai and the sea there are Qing and Qi in their own right—it is not that there is no territory."
translations.idiomatic: Between the Huai and the sea Qing and Qi still stand—we are not without territory."

sentences.zh: 又問：「蒼梧何故遂加斬戮？」

translations.literal: They asked again, "Why was Cangwu then put to the sword?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked further: "Why was Prince Cangwu executed outright?"

sentences.zh: 僧朗曰：「蒼梧暴虐，書契未聞，武王斬紂，懸之黃鉞，共是所聞，何傷於義？」

translations.literal: Senglang said, "Cangwu was violent and cruel beyond anything recorded; King Wu beheaded Zhou and displayed him on the yellow battle-axe—both are matters we have heard of; how does this harm righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: Senglang said: "Cangwu's cruelty exceeds anything in the records; King Wu slew Zhou and displayed his head on the yellow axe—both are matters of record. Where is the injury to righteousness?"

sentences.zh: 昇明中，北使殷靈誕、苟昭先在虜，聞太祖登極，靈誕謂虜典客曰：「宋魏通好，憂患是同。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era, the northern envoys Yin Lingdan and Gou Zhaoxian were among the barbarians; hearing that the Founding Emperor had ascended the throne, Lingdan said to the barbarian Master of Guests, "Song and Wei were on good terms and shared the same troubles.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengming, envoys Yin Lingdan and Gou Zhaoxian were detained in the north. When they heard the Founding Emperor had taken the throne, Lingdan told the Wei Master of Guests: "Song and Wei were allies who shared common perils.

sentences.zh: 宋今滅亡，魏不相救，何用和親？」

translations.literal: Song is now destroyed—if Wei does not rescue it, what use is marriage alliance?"
translations.idiomatic: Song is now destroyed and Wei did not save it—of what use is alliance by marriage?"

sentences.zh: 及虜寇豫州，靈誕因請為劉昶司馬，不獲。

translations.literal: When the barbarians raided Yu Province, Lingdan therefore requested to serve as Liu Chang's marshal but was not granted this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei invaded Yu Province, Lingdan asked to serve as Liu Chang's marshal but was refused.

sentences.zh: 僧朗至北，虜置之靈誕下，僧朗立席言曰：「靈誕昔是宋使，今成齊民。

translations.literal: When Senglang reached the north, the barbarians seated him below Lingdan; Senglang rose from his mat and said, "Lingdan was once an envoy of Song; he is now a subject of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Senglang arrived in the north, the Wei seated him below Lingdan. Senglang rose and said: "Lingdan was once Song's envoy; he is now a subject of Qi.

sentences.zh: 實希魏主以禮見處。」

translations.literal: I truly hope the lord of Wei will treat him with courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: I trust the Wei ruler will treat him with courtesy."

sentences.zh: 靈誕交言，遂相忿詈，調虜曰：「使臣不能立節本朝，誠自慙恨。」

translations.literal: Lingdan exchanged words and they then reviled each other in anger; he said to the barbarians, "This envoy could not uphold his integrity for his court—I am truly ashamed and regretful."
translations.idiomatic: Lingdan answered hotly and they traded insults. He told the Wei: "This envoy failed his court in loyalty—I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 劉昶賂客解奉君於會刺殺僧朗，虜即收奉君誅之，殯斂僧朗，送喪隨靈誕等南歸，厚加贈賻。

translations.literal: Liu Chang bribed a guest to have Xie Fengjun assassinate Senglang at a gathering; the barbarians immediately seized Fengjun and executed him, encoffined Senglang, sent the funeral to follow Lingdan and others south, and gave lavish funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang bribed an agent to have Xie Fengjun assassinate Senglang at a banquet. The Wei seized Fengjun and executed him, prepared Senglang's body for burial, sent the funeral south with Lingdan's party, and granted lavish compensation.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，昭先具以啟聞，靈誕下獄死，贈僧朗散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Zhaoxian reported everything in full; Lingdan was imprisoned and died; Senglang was posthumously given the title Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Steeds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor ascended the throne, Zhaoxian reported the full story; Lingdan died in prison; Senglang was posthumously made Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Steeds.

sentences.zh: 冬，遣驍騎將軍劉纘、前軍將軍張謨使虜。

translations.literal: In winter, Swift Cavalry General Liu Zuan and Vanguard General Zhang Mo were sent as envoys to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Swift Cavalry General Liu Zuan and Vanguard General Zhang Mo were dispatched as envoys to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，虜使李道固報聘，世祖於玄武湖水步軍講武，登龍舟引見之。

translations.literal: The next winter the barbarian envoy Li Daogu returned the visit; the Founding Emperor reviewed the naval forces on Xuanwu Lake, boarded the dragon boat, and received him.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter the Wei envoy Li Daogu came on a return visit; the Founding Emperor reviewed naval forces on Xuanwu Lake, boarded the dragon boat, and received him.

sentences.zh: 自此歲使往來，疆埸無事。

translations.literal: From this time envoys came and went each year, and the borders were untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter envoys exchanged visits yearly and the frontier remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 三年，初令鄰里黨各置一長，五家為隣，五隣為里，五里為黨。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was first ordered that each neighborhood and ward should appoint one head; five households made a neighbor-group, five neighbor-groups a hamlet, five hamlets a ward.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the state first ordered each ward to appoint a head: five households formed a neighborhood, five neighborhoods a hamlet, five hamlets a ward.

sentences.zh: 四年，造戶籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year household registers were compiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year household registers were drawn up.

sentences.zh: 分置州郡，雍州、涼州、秦州、沙州、涇州、華州、岐州、河州、西華州、寧州、陝州、洛州、荊州、郢州、北豫州、東荊州、南豫州、西兖州、東兖州、南徐州、東徐州、青州、齊州、濟州二十五州在河南；

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies were divided and set up: Yong, Liang, Qin, Sha, Jing, Hua, Qi, He, Xihua, Ning, Shan, Luo, Jing, Ying, North Yu, East Jing, South Yu, West Yan, East Yan, South Xu, East Xu, Qing, Qi, and Ji—twenty-five provinces south of the Yellow River;
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies were reorganized: Yong, Liang, Qin, Sha, Jing, Hua, Qi, He, Xihua, Ning, Shan, Luo, Jing, Ying, North Yu, East Jing, South Yu, West Yan, East Yan, South Xu, East Xu, Qing, Qi, and Ji—twenty-five provinces south of the Yellow River;

translations.literal: (Xiang)
translations.idiomatic: (Xiang)

sentences.zh: 〔相〕州、懷州、

translations.literal: [Xiang] Province, Huai Province,
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Province, Huai Province,

translations.literal: (Qin)
translations.idiomatic: (Qin)

sentences.zh: 〔汾〕州、東雍州、肆州、定州、瀛州、朔州、并州、冀州、幽州、平州、司州十三州在河北。

translations.literal: [Fen] Province, East Yong, Si, Ding, Ying, Shuo, Bing, Ji, You, Ping, and Si—thirteen provinces north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Fen Province, East Yong, Si, Ding, Ying, Shuo, Bing, Ji, You, Ping, and Si—thirteen provinces north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 凡分魏、晉舊司、豫、青、兖、冀、并、幽、秦、雍、涼十州地，及宋所失淮北為三十八州矣。

translations.literal: In all, the old territories of Wei and Jin in the ten provinces of Si, Yu, Qing, Yan, Ji, Bing, You, Qin, Yong, and Liang, together with the north of the Huai lost by Song, were divided into thirty-eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether the former Wei and Jin lands of Si, Yu, Qing, Yan, Ji, Bing, You, Qin, Yong, and Liang, together with the Huai-north territories Song had lost, were reorganized into thirty-eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 明年，邊人桓天生作亂，虜遣步騎萬餘人助之，至比陽，為征虜將軍戴僧靜等所破。

translations.literal: The next year the frontier man Huan Tiansheng rebelled; the barbarians sent more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to assist him; reaching Biyang, they were defeated by Pacifier of the Barbarians General Dai Sengjing and others.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the frontier leader Huan Tiansheng rose in revolt; the Wei sent more than ten thousand foot and horse to his aid, but at Biyang they were routed by Pacifier of the Barbarians Dai Sengjing and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 荒人胡丘生起義懸瓠，為虜所擊，戰敗南奔。

translations.literal: The frontier man Hu Qiuji raised rebellion at Xuancheng; he was struck by the barbarians, defeated in battle, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier leader Hu Qiuji rebelled at Xuancheng, was beaten by the Wei, and fled south in defeat.

sentences.zh: 偽安南將軍遼東公、平南將軍上谷公又攻舞陰，舞陰戍主輔國將軍殷公愍拒破之。

translations.literal: The false General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Liaodong, and General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Shanggu, again attacked Wuyin; the garrison commander of Wuyin, Support-the-State General Yin Gongmin, resisted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifier of the South, Duke of Liaodong, and the Pacifier of the South, Duke of Shanggu, attacked Wuyin again; the garrison commander Yin Gongmin, Support-the-State General, held the city and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 六年，虜又遣眾助桓天生，與輔國將軍曹虎戰，大敗於隔城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the barbarians again sent troops to aid Huan Tiansheng; they fought Support-the-State General Cao Hu and were greatly defeated at Gecheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Wei again sent troops to aid Huan Tiansheng; they met Support-the-State General Cao Hu and suffered a crushing defeat at Gecheng.

sentences.zh: 至七年，遣使邢產、侯靈紹復通好。

translations.literal: By the seventh year envoys Xing Chan and Hou Lingshao were sent to restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year envoys Xing Chan and Hou Lingshao were dispatched to renew friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 先是劉纘再使虜，太后馮氏悅而親之。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Zuan had again been envoy to the barbarians; Empress Dowager Feng was pleased and treated him with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Zuan had again served as envoy to the Wei; Empress Dowager Feng took a liking to him and received him warmly.

sentences.zh: 馮氏有計略，作皇誥十八篇，偽左僕射李思沖稱史臣注解。

translations.literal: Feng had stratagems and composed eighteen chapters of Imperial Admonitions; the false Left Vice Director Li Sichong styled himself historiographer and annotated them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng was resourceful and composed eighteen chapters of Imperial Admonitions; the Left Vice Director Li Sichong signed himself as historiographer and supplied commentary.

sentences.zh: 是歲，馮氏死。

translations.literal: That year Feng died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lady Feng died.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖還隔城所俘獲二千餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Founding Emperor returned more than two thousand captives taken at Gecheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Founding Emperor repatriated more than two thousand captives taken at Gecheng.

sentences.zh: 佛狸已來，稍僭華典，胡風國俗，雜相揉亂。

translations.literal: Since Foli's time they had gradually usurped Chinese institutions; barbarian customs and national usages were mixed and confused together.
translations.idiomatic: Since Foli's reign they had gradually adopted Chinese institutions, while barbarian custom and state usage intermingled in confusion.

sentences.zh: 宏知談義，解屬文，輕果有遠略。

translations.literal: Hong understood discourse on principles, could compose literary pieces, was quick and resolute, and had far-reaching designs.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was versed in philosophical discourse and literary composition, quick and decisive, with far-reaching designs.

sentences.zh: 遊河北至比干墓，作弔比干文云：「脫非武發，封墓誰因？

translations.literal: Traveling north of the river to the tomb of Bigan, he composed an elegy for Bigan saying, "If not for King Wu's rise, by whom would the tomb have been sealed?
translations.idiomatic: On a tour north of the Yellow River he came to Bigan's tomb and wrote an elegy: "Had King Wu not risen, who would have sealed this grave?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: （分土）

translations.literal: (divided earth)
translations.idiomatic: (divided earth)

sentences.zh: 〔介士〕，胡不我臣！」

translations.literal: [loyal knight], why do you not serve me!"
translations.idiomatic: [loyal knight]—why will you not be my minister!"

sentences.zh: 宏以己巳歲立圓丘、方澤，置三夫人、九嬪。

translations.literal: In a jisi year Hong established the Round Mound and Square Pond altars and appointed three Ladies and nine Imperial Concubines.
translations.idiomatic: In a jisi year Hong established the Round Mound and Square Pond altars and appointed three chief consorts and nine imperial concubines.

sentences.zh: 平城南有干水，出定襄堺，流入海，去城五十里，世號為索干都。

translations.literal: South of Pingcheng is the Gan River, rising from the border of Dingxiang and flowing into the sea; fifty li from the city, it was generationally called Suogan Du.
translations.idiomatic: South of Pingcheng runs the Gan River, which rises in Dingxiang and flows to the sea; fifty li from the city it was known as Suogan Du.

sentences.zh: 土氣寒凝，風砂恒起，六月雨雪。

translations.literal: The soil and air were cold and congealed; wind and sand constantly rose; in the sixth month there was snow and rain.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was bitterly cold, sandstorms constant, and snow fell even in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 議遷都洛京。

translations.literal: They debated moving the capital to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated relocating the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣使李道固、蔣少游報使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year envoys Li Daogu and Jiang Shaoyou returned the visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year envoys Li Daogu and Jiang Shaoyou came on a return mission.

sentences.zh: 少游有機巧，密令觀京師宮殿楷式。

translations.literal: Shaoyou was ingenious; he was secretly ordered to observe the models of the capital's palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou was clever with his hands; he was secretly instructed to study the layout of the capital palaces.

sentences.zh: 清河崔元祖啟世祖曰：「少游，臣之外甥，特有公輸之思。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanzu of Qinghe memorialized the Founding Emperor, saying, "Shaoyou is my sister's son and has the ingenuity of Gongshu Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanzu of Qinghe wrote to the Founding Emperor: "Shaoyou is my sister's son and possesses the ingenuity of Gongshu Ban.

sentences.zh: 宋世陷虜，處以大匠之官。

translations.literal: In Song times he fell captive among the barbarians and was placed in the office of master craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Captured in Song times, he was made chief craftsman among the Wei.

sentences.zh: 今為副使，必欲模範宮闕。

translations.literal: Now as deputy envoy he is certain to take the palace as his model.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy envoy he will surely copy our palace models.

sentences.zh: 豈可令氈鄉之鄙，取象天宮？

translations.literal: How can the rustic felt-tent country be allowed to imitate the Heavenly Palace?
translations.idiomatic: How can we let a felt-tent frontier copy the celestial palace?

sentences.zh: 臣謂且留少游，令使主反命。」

translations.literal: I submit that Shaoyou be detained and the chief envoy sent back to report."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that Shaoyou be detained while the chief envoy returns to deliver his report.

sentences.zh: 世祖以非和通意，不許。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, deeming this contrary to the spirit of reconciliation, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, judging this incompatible with good relations, refused.

sentences.zh: 少游，安樂人。

translations.literal: Shaoyou was a native of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou came from Anle.

sentences.zh: 虜宮室制度，皆從其出。

translations.literal: The barbarians' palace regulations all issued from him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei palace system owed everything to his designs.

sentences.zh: 初，佛狸討羯胡於長安，殺道人且盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Foli campaigned against the Jie Hu in Chang'an, he killed the Buddhist monks nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: When Foli campaigned against the Jie Hu in Chang'an, he slaughtered the Buddhist clergy almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 及元嘉南寇，獲道人，以鐵籠盛之。

translations.literal: During the Yuanjia southern raid he captured monks and kept them in iron cages.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia invasion he captured monks and confined them in iron cages.

sentences.zh: 後佛狸感惡疾，自是敬畏佛教，立塔寺浮圖。

translations.literal: Later Foli suffered a malignant illness; from this time he revered Buddhism and erected pagodas and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Later Foli fell gravely ill; thereafter he revered Buddhism and built pagodas and temples.

sentences.zh: 宏父弘禪位後，黃冠素服，持戒誦經，居石窟寺。

translations.literal: After Hong, Hong's father, abdicated, he wore yellow caps and plain robes, kept the precepts and chanted sutras, and dwelt at the Stone Grotto Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After abdicating, Hong's father wore Daoist caps and plain robes, kept the precepts, chanted sutras, and lived at the Stone Grotto Temple.

sentences.zh: 宏，道人法秀與苟兒王阿辱瑰王等謀反，事覺，囚法秀，加以籠頭鐵鏁，無故自解脫，虜穿其頸骨，使呪之曰：「若復有神，當令穿肉不入。」

translations.literal: Under Hong, the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion with King Gou'er, King Arugui, and others; when the affair was discovered, Faxiu was imprisoned, fitted with an iron cage and chains, yet freed himself without cause; the barbarians pierced his neck bone and made him curse, saying, "If you truly have divine power, let the piercing not enter the flesh."
translations.idiomatic: Under Hong the monk Faxiu conspired with King Gou'er, King Arugui, and others; when exposed he was imprisoned in an iron cage and shackles, yet broke free unaided; the Wei pierced his neck and bade him swear: "If you have divine power, let the blade not pierce your flesh."

sentences.zh: 遂穿而殉之，三日乃死。

translations.literal: They pierced through and executed him; after three days he died.
translations.idiomatic: They pierced him through and put him to death; he lingered three days before dying.

sentences.zh: 偽咸陽王復欲盡殺道人，太后馮氏不許。

translations.literal: The false Prince of Xianyang again wished to kill all the monks, but Empress Dowager Feng would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xianyang again sought to slaughter all monks, but Empress Dowager Feng forbade it.

sentences.zh: 宏尤精信，粗涉義理，宮殿內立浮圖。

translations.literal: Hong was especially devout, had rough acquaintance with doctrine, and erected pagodas within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was deeply devout, had some grasp of doctrine, and built pagodas within the palace.

sentences.zh: 宏既經古洛，是歲下偽詔尚書思慎曰：「夫覆載垂化，必由四氣運其功；

translations.literal: After Hong had toured ancient Luoyang, that year he issued a false edict to the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Si Shen, saying, "Heaven and earth spread forth transformation; it must be through the four seasons that their work is carried out;
translations.idiomatic: After touring ancient Luoyang, Hong that year addressed Director Si Shen in an edict: "Heaven and earth unfold their transforming power only through the working of the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 曦曜望舒，亦須五星助其暉。

translations.literal: The sun and moon likewise need the five stars to aid their radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon likewise need the five planets to lend their brilliance.

sentences.zh: 仰惟聖母，睿識自天，業高曠古，將稽詳典範，日新皇度。

translations.literal: Looking up to the holy mother, her sage insight is heaven-given, her achievement towers above antiquity; she will examine and follow the canonical models, renewing the imperial measure day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the holy mother: her wisdom is heaven-sent, her achievement towers over antiquity; she will consult the canonical models and renew the imperial order day by day.

sentences.zh: 不圖罪逆招禍，奄丁窮罰，追惟罔極，永無逮及。

translations.literal: Never did we expect that treason would invite disaster; suddenly she met the ultimate punishment. Reflecting on this, grief knows no bounds — never again can we reach her.
translations.idiomatic: We never imagined that crime and rebellion would bring such calamity; suddenly she suffered the final penalty. Looking back, our sorrow is boundless — we can never reach her again.

sentences.zh: 思遵先旨，勑造明堂之樣。

translations.literal: Thinking to follow the late intent, I command the making of a model of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of her last wishes, I order that a model of the Bright Hall be prepared.

sentences.zh: 卿所制體含六合，事越中古，理圓義備，可軌之千載。

translations.literal: The design you have made embraces the six directions; in practice it surpasses middle antiquity; its principles are rounded and its rites complete — it may serve as a model for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The form you have devised encompasses the six directions, surpasses the standards of middle antiquity, and is complete in principle and rite — a pattern that may guide us for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 信是應世之材，先固之器也。

translations.literal: Truly this is talent fit for the age, an instrument that will long endure.
translations.idiomatic: You are truly a man for the times, a pillar that will stand firm for generations.

sentences.zh: 羣臣瞻見模樣，莫不僉然欲速造，朕以寡昧，亦思造盛禮。

translations.literal: When the ministers gazed upon the model, all agreed they wished to build it quickly; I, though lacking in wisdom, also wish to undertake this great rite.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers saw the model, all agreed they wanted it built at once; I too, though unlearned, wish to perform this great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 卿可即於今歲停宮城之作，營建此構，興皇代之奇制，遠成先志，近副朕懷。」

translations.literal: You may at once this year halt work on the palace city and construct this building, raising an extraordinary design for our dynasty — fulfilling the late intent from afar and matching my heart from near.
translations.idiomatic: This year you shall suspend work on the palace city and build this structure instead, raising an extraordinary monument for our dynasty — fulfilling her distant wish and satisfying my present desire.

sentences.zh: 又詔公卿參定刑律。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict for the ministers and nobles to jointly revise the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the ministers and nobles to collaborate on revising the penal statutes.

sentences.zh: 又詔罷臈前儺，唯年一儺。

translations.literal: He also decreed to abolish the pre-Laba exorcism rite, keeping only one exorcism per year.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished the pre-Laba exorcism, retaining only one annual exorcism rite.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「季冬朝賀，典無成文，以袴褶事非禮敬之謂，若置寒朝服，徒成煩濁，自今罷小歲賀，歲初一賀。」

translations.literal: He also decreed: "Winter-end court congratulations have no established precedent. Since wearing military dress is not what propriety and reverence require, and setting out cold-season court robes would only create needless bother, from now on the minor New Year congratulations are abolished — there shall be one congratulation at the New Year."
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed: "There is no fixed precedent for winter-end court congratulations. Military dress is not what ritual decorum calls for, and issuing cold-weather court robes would only add needless trouble. Henceforth the minor New Year audience is abolished; there shall be a single New Year audience each year."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「王爵非庶姓所僭，伯號是五等常秩。

translations.literal: He also decreed: "The title of king is not to be usurped by common surnames; the rank of earl is the regular grade of the five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed: "The title of king is not for common clans to assume; the rank of earl is the standing grade within the five ranks.

sentences.zh: 烈祖之冑，仍本王爵，其餘王皆為公，〔公〕轉為侯，侯即為伯，子男如舊。

translations.literal: Descendants of the Founding Ancestor shall retain the original kingly title; all other kings become dukes, dukes become marquises, marquises become earls, viscounts and barons as before.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the Founding Ancestor keep their original royal titles; all other kings become dukes, dukes become marquises, marquises become earls, and viscounts and barons remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 雖名易於本，而品不異昔。

translations.literal: Although the titles change from their originals, the grades do not differ from before.
translations.idiomatic: Though the names differ from what they were, the ranks themselves remain as before.

sentences.zh: 公第一品，侯第二品，伯第三品，子第四品，男第五品。」

translations.literal: Duke is first rank, marquis second, earl third, viscount fourth, baron fifth."
translations.idiomatic: Duke is first rank, marquis second, earl third, viscount fourth, and baron fifth."

sentences.zh: 十年，上遣司徒參軍蕭琛、范雲北使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the emperor sent Staff Officers Xiao Chen and Fan Yun on a mission to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the emperor dispatched Staff Officers Xiao Chen and Fan Yun as envoys to the north.

sentences.zh: 宏西郊，即前祠天壇處也。

translations.literal: Hong [performed the rite at the] western suburbs — the former site of the heaven-worship altar.
translations.idiomatic: Hong worshipped at the western suburbs, the same place where the heaven altar had stood before.

sentences.zh: 宏與偽公卿從二十餘騎戎服繞壇，宏一周，公卿七匝，謂之蹋壇。

translations.literal: Hong and the pseudo ministers, with some twenty mounted followers in military dress, circled the altar — Hong one circuit, the ministers seven circuits; this was called "treading the altar."
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the pseudo court ministers, with more than twenty mounted attendants in military dress, circled the altar — Hong once, the ministers seven times — in what was called "treading the altar."

sentences.zh: 明日，復戎服登壇祠天，宏又繞三匝，公卿七匝，謂之繞天。

translations.literal: The next day, again in military dress they mounted the altar to worship Heaven; Hong circled three circuits, the ministers seven — this was called "encircling Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, again in military dress they ascended the altar to worship Heaven; Hong circled three times and the ministers seven — this was called "encircling Heaven."

sentences.zh: 以繩相交絡，紐木枝棖，覆以青繒，形制平圓，下容百人坐，謂之為「繖」，一云「百子帳」也。

translations.literal: Ropes were interlaced, wooden branches bound and tied, covered with green silk; the shape was flat and round, with room below for a hundred people to sit — they called it an "umbrella"; others say "the tent of a hundred sons."
translations.idiomatic: Ropes were woven together, wooden poles lashed and braced, and the whole covered with green silk; the structure was flat and round, with space below for a hundred people to sit. They called it an "umbrella," or alternatively a "hundred-sons tent."

sentences.zh: 於此下宴息。

translations.literal: Below this they feasted and rested.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath it they held their feast and rested.

sentences.zh: 次祠廟及布政明堂，皆引朝廷使人觀視。

translations.literal: Next they worshipped at the ancestral temple and displayed governance at the Bright Hall, in each case inviting the envoys from the southern court to observe.
translations.idiomatic: They then worshipped at the ancestral temple and displayed governance at the Bright Hall, each time inviting the southern court's envoys to watch.

sentences.zh: 每使至，宏親相應接，申以言義。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys arrived, Hong personally received them and expounded upon principles of discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys arrived, Hong received them in person and discoursed on matters of principle.

sentences.zh: 甚重齊人，常謂其臣下曰：「江南多好臣。」

translations.literal: He greatly respected men of Qi, often telling his ministers: "South of the Yangtze has many fine ministers."
translations.idiomatic: He held men of Qi in high regard and often told his ministers, "South of the Yangtze has many excellent ministers."

sentences.zh: 偽侍臣李元凱對曰：「江南多好臣，歲一易主；

translations.literal: The pseudo attendant Li Yuankai replied: "South of the Yangtze has many fine ministers — they change their lord every year;
translations.idiomatic: The pseudo attendant Li Yuankai replied, "South of the Yangtze has many fine ministers — they change their ruler every year;

sentences.zh: 江北無好臣，而百年一主。」

translations.literal: North of the Yangtze has no fine ministers, yet one lord lasts a hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: north of the Yangtze has no fine ministers, yet one ruler endures for a hundred years."

sentences.zh: 宏大慙，出元凱為雍州長史，俄召復職。

translations.literal: Hong was deeply ashamed. He sent Yuankai out as Chief Administrator of Yong Province, then soon recalled him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was deeply embarrassed. He posted Yuankai to Yong Province as chief administrator, then soon recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，治白下，謂人曰：「我欲以此城為上頓處。」

translations.literal: Early in the reign of Emperor Wu, [Hong] developed Baixia and told people: "I wish to use this city as my advance staging place."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Wu, Hong developed Baixia and told others, "I intend to use this city as my forward staging base."

sentences.zh: 後於石頭造

translations.literal: Later at Shitou he had built
translations.idiomatic: Later at Shitou he constructed

translations.literal: (Spirit) [emended: open]
translations.idiomatic: open

sentences.zh: 〔露〕車三千乘，欲步道取彭城，形迹頗著。

translations.literal: open carts, three thousand in number, intending to march overland to take Pengcheng; his intentions became quite evident.
translations.idiomatic: three thousand open carts, planning to reach Pengcheng by land march; his designs became quite obvious.

sentences.zh: 先是八年北使顏幼明、劉思斅反命，偽南部尚書李思沖曰：「二國之和，義在庇民。

translations.literal: Previously, when in the eighth year the northern envoys Yan Youming and Liu Siqiao returned from their mission, the pseudo Director of the Southern Department Li Sichong said: "Harmony between our two states lies in protecting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the eighth-year northern envoys Yan Youming and Liu Siqiao returned, the pseudo Director of the Southern Department Li Sichong said, "Peace between our two states exists to shelter the people.

sentences.zh: 如聞南朝大造舟車，欲侵淮、泗，推心相期，何應如此？」

translations.literal: I hear the southern court is greatly building boats and chariots, intending to invade the Huai and Si regions. We trusted each other sincerely — how could this be?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear the southern court is building ships and chariots on a large scale, intending to strike the Huai and Si. We pledged our hearts to one another — how could this be?"

sentences.zh: 幼明曰：「主上方弘大信於天下，不失臣妾。

translations.literal: Youming said: "Our sovereign is now spreading great trust throughout the realm, loyal to the utmost as lord and vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Youming said, "Our sovereign is now extending great good faith throughout the realm, never failing in the bond between lord and subject.

sentences.zh: 既與輯和，何容二三其德？

translations.literal: Now that we have made peace, how could we waver in our integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have restored harmony, how could we be double-dealing?

sentences.zh: 壃埸之言，差不足信。

translations.literal: Rumors from the border are hardly to be credited.
translations.idiomatic: Reports from the frontier are scarcely to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷若必

translations.literal: Moreover, if the court should truly
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if the court were truly to

sentences.zh: （恭恕）

translations.literal: (respectful and forbearing) [emended: furious wrath]
translations.idiomatic: fly into furious wrath

sentences.zh: 〔赫怒〕，使守在外，亦不近相淮濆。」

translations.literal: fly into furious wrath, the garrisons are posted abroad and would not approach each other near the Huai banks."
translations.idiomatic: fly into furious wrath, the frontier garrisons are stationed far afield and would not draw near each other along the Huai."

sentences.zh: 思沖曰：「我國之彊，經略淮東，何患不蕩海東岳，政存於信誓耳。

translations.literal: Sichong said: "Our state's strength — if we set out to take the Huai east, what worry have we that we could not sweep away the eastern sea and Mt. Heng? It all depends on keeping faith in our pledged word.
translations.idiomatic: Sichong said, "Our state is strong; if we planned to advance east of the Huai, what would prevent us from sweeping to the eastern sea and Mt. Heng? All that matters is keeping our pledged word.

sentences.zh: 且和好既結，豈可復有不信？

translations.literal: Besides, now that amity is established, how could there be fresh distrust?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, now that friendship is established, how could distrust arise again?

sentences.zh: 昔華元、子反，戰伐之際，尚能以誠相告，此意良慕也。」

translations.literal: Long ago Hua Yuan and Zifan, even amid warfare, could still speak to each other in sincerity — this is truly admirable."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Hua Yuan and Zifan, even in the midst of battle, could still speak to each other with sincerity — that spirit is truly worth emulating."

sentences.zh: 幼明曰：「卿未有子反之急，詎求登床之請？」

translations.literal: Youming said: "You are not in Zifan's desperate plight — why seek the favor of being invited to the couch?"
translations.idiomatic: Youming said, "You are not in Zifan's desperate straits — why ask for the privilege of sharing his couch?"

sentences.zh: 是後宏亦欲南侵徐、豫，於淮、泗間大積馬蒭。

translations.literal: After this Hong also wished to invade the south at Xu and Yu, and greatly accumulated horse fodder between the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: After this Hong also planned a southern invasion of Xu and Yu, stockpiling horse fodder in great quantities between the Huai and Si.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣露布并上書，稱當南寇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he sent open proclamations and a memorial, stating that he would invade south.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he issued open proclamations and a memorial announcing that he would raid the south.

sentences.zh: 世祖發揚、徐州民丁，廣設召募。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu mobilized the conscript population of Yang and Xu provinces and widely opened recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu mobilized the conscript levies of Yang and Xu provinces and greatly expanded recruitment.

sentences.zh: 北地人支酉，聚數千人，於長安城北西山起義。

translations.literal: Zhi You of Beidi, gathering several thousand men, raised a revolt on Western Mountain north of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi You of Beidi gathered several thousand men and rose in rebellion on Western Mountain north of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 遣使告梁州刺史陰智伯。

translations.literal: He sent messengers to inform Yin Zhibo, Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to notify Yin Zhibo, Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 秦州人王度人起義應酉，攻獲偽刺史劉藻，秦、雍間七州民皆響震，眾至十萬，各自保壁，望朝廷救其兵。

translations.literal: Wang Duren of Qin Province rose in revolt to join You, attacking and capturing the pseudo Governor Liu Zao. The people of seven provinces between Qin and Yong all echoed in alarm; their forces reached a hundred thousand, each holding their own fortified walls, hoping the court would send troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duren of Qin Province rebelled in support of You, attacking and capturing the pseudo Governor Liu Zao. The people of seven provinces between Qin and Yong rose in response; their forces reached a hundred thousand, each holding fortified walls and awaiting imperial relief.

sentences.zh: 宏遣弟偽河南王幹、尚書盧陽烏擊秦、雍義軍，幹大敗。

translations.literal: Hong sent his brother, the pseudo Prince of Henan Gan, and the Director Lu Yangwu to strike the loyalist army of Qin and Yong; Gan was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent his brother, the pseudo Prince of Henan Gan, and Director Lu Yangwu to attack the loyalist forces in Qin and Yong; Gan suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 酉迎戰，進至咸陽北濁谷，圍偽司空長洛王繆老生，合戰，又大破之，老生走還長安。
