translations.literal: You met them in battle, advancing to Turbid Valley north of Xianyang, besieging the pseudo Minister of Works, Prince of Changluo Miao Laosheng. In the general engagement he again routed them; Laosheng fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: You gave battle, advancing to Turbid Valley north of Xianyang and besieging the pseudo Minister of Works, Prince of Changluo Miao Laosheng. In the general engagement he routed them again, and Laosheng fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史陰智伯遣軍主席德仁、張弘林等數千人應接酉等，進向長安，所至皆靡。

translations.literal: Governor Yin Zhibo of Liang Province sent Commanders Xi Deren, Zhang Honglin, and several thousand men to support You and the others, advancing on Chang'an; wherever they went, all yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhibo, Governor of Liang Province, sent Commanders Xi Deren and Zhang Honglin with several thousand men to join You's forces and advance on Chang'an; everywhere they went, resistance collapsed.

sentences.zh: 會世祖崩，宏聞關中危急，乃稱聞喪退師。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Wu died; Hong, hearing that Guanzhong was in crisis, claimed he was halting the campaign upon hearing of the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Emperor Wu died. Hong, learning that Guanzhong was in peril, announced that he was withdrawing his army upon hearing of the mourning.

sentences.zh: 八月，使持節、安南大將軍、都督徐青齊三州諸軍事、南中郎將、徐州刺史、廣陵侯府長史、帶淮陽太守鹿樹生移齊兖州府長史府：「奉被行所尚書符騰詔：『皇師雷舉，搖旆南指，誓清江祲，志廓衡靄。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Envoy bearing credentials, General Who Pacifies the South, Commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Xu, Qing, and Qi provinces, Captain of the Southern Gentlemen, Chief Administrator of the palace of the Marquis of Guangling [with concurrent appointment as] Administrator of Huaiyang Lu Shusheng addressed the Chief Administrator's office of Yan Province in Qi: "I have received the command transmitted by the Office of the Director of the Department carried in the official dispatch: 'The imperial army thunders forth, banners sway southward; we vow to cleanse the Yangtze of calamity and aim to clear the mists from Mt. Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Lu Shusheng — envoy bearing credentials, General Who Pacifies the South, Commander-in-chief of military affairs in Xu, Qing, and Qi provinces, Captain of the Southern Gentlemen, Chief Administrator of the Marquis of Guangling's household, and concurrent Administrator of Huaiyang — addressed the Chief Administrator's office of Yan Province in Qi: "I have received the command transmitted by the Office of the Director of the Department in the official dispatch: 'The imperial army thunders forth, banners turn southward; we swear to cleanse the Yangtze of evil and to clear away the mists of Mt. Heng.

sentences.zh: 以去月下旬，濟次河洛。

translations.literal: Last month, toward month's end, we crossed the [Yellow] River and halted at the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the end of last month we crossed the river and encamped at the Luo.

sentences.zh: 會前使人邢巒等至，審知彼有大艾。

translations.literal: When the earlier envoy Xing Luan and others arrived, we verified that they had suffered a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the earlier envoys Xing Luan and others arrived, we learned that they had suffered a great bereavement.

sentences.zh: 以春秋之義，聞喪寢伐。

translations.literal: In accordance with the Spring and Autumn principle, upon hearing of mourning one halts warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals, upon hearing of mourning one ceases campaigning.

sentences.zh: 爰勑有司，輟鑾止軔，休馬華陽，戢戈嵩北。

translations.literal: Accordingly I command the officials: halt the imperial carriage and draw rein, rest the horses at Huayang, and sheathe the weapons north of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly I have ordered the officials to halt the imperial carriage and draw rein, rest the horses at Huayang, and sheathe the weapons north of Song.

sentences.zh: 便肇經周制，光宅中區，永皇基于無窮，恢盛業乎萬祀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he will initiate the rites of Zhou, illuminate the central realm, establish the imperial foundation forever, and extend the glorious enterprise for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He will then inaugurate the rites of Zhou, bring light to the central realm, establish the imperial foundation for eternity, and extend this glorious enterprise for ten thousand generations.

translations.literal: (chen) [emended: imperial throne]
translations.idiomatic: imperial throne

sentences.zh: 〔宸〕居重正，鴻化增新，四海承休，莫不銘慶。』

translations.literal: The imperial residence holds secure the orthodox succession; the great transforming power is daily renewed; the four seas receive felicity — none fail to inscribe this joy.'
translations.idiomatic: The imperial throne holds firm the orthodox succession; the great transforming power grows ever new; the four seas receive blessings, and all inscribe this rejoicing.'

sentences.zh: 故以往示如律令。」

translations.literal: Therefore [this] is sent forth as notification — let it be executed according to decree."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore this is sent forth for your information — let it be carried out as decreed."

sentences.zh: 并遣使弔國諱。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to offer condolences for the state's mourning taboo [the late emperor's death].
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to offer condolences on the state's bereavement.

sentences.zh: 遣偽大將楊大眼、張聰明等數萬人攻酉，酉、廣等竝見殺，

translations.literal: [Hong] sent the pseudo generals Yang Dayan, Zhang Congming, and tens of thousands of men to attack You; You, Guang, and others were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent the pseudo generals Yang Dayan and Zhang Congming with tens of thousands of men to attack You; You, Guang, and the others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 遣司徒參軍劉斅、車騎參軍沈宏報使至北。

translations.literal: [The court] sent Staff Officer Liu Jiao of the Department of State Affairs and Cavalry Attendant Shen Hong as return envoys to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Staff Officer Liu Jiao of the Department of State Affairs and Cavalry Attendant Shen Hong as return envoys to the north.

sentences.zh: 宏稱字玄覽。

translations.literal: Hong styled himself Xuanlan ("Profound View").
translations.idiomatic: Hong used the style Xuanlan, "Profound View."

sentences.zh: 其夏，虜平北將軍魯直清率眾降，以為督洛州軍事，領平戎校尉、征虜將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: That summer, the Northern Wei general Lu Zhiqing of Pingbei surrendered with his force. [Hong] appointed him to supervise military affairs in Luo Province, with concurrent titles as Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Northern Wei general Lu Zhiqing of Pingbei surrendered with his troops. Hong appointed him to supervise military affairs in Luo Province, with concurrent titles as Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and Governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，宏徙都洛陽，改姓元氏。

translations.literal: That year Hong moved the capital to Luoyang and changed the surname to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hong moved the capital to Luoyang and changed the imperial surname to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 初，匈奴女名托跋，妻李陵，胡俗以母名為姓，故虜為李陵之後，虜甚諱之，有言其是陵後者，輒見殺，至是乃改姓焉。

translations.literal: Initially there was a Xiongnu woman named Tuoba who married Li Ling; by barbarian custom the mother's name was taken as surname, so the Northern Wei were said to be descendants of Li Ling. They greatly tabooed this — whoever said they were Li Ling's descendants was immediately killed. Only now did they change the surname.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago a Xiongnu woman named Tuoba married Li Ling; by barbarian custom the mother's name became the clan name, so the Northern Wei were said to be Li Ling's descendants. They fiercely suppressed this claim — anyone who said they were Li Ling's heirs was put to death. Only now did they change the surname.

sentences.zh: 宏聞高宗踐阼非正，既新移都，兼欲大示威力。

translations.literal: Hong heard that Emperor Ming's accession was irregular; having recently moved the capital, he also wished to display his might on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Hong heard that Emperor Ming's accession was illegitimate; having just moved the capital, he also wished to display his power on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 是冬，自率大眾分寇豫、徐、司、梁四州。

translations.literal: That winter he personally led a great host in divided raids on the four provinces Yu, Xu, Si, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he personally led a great army in divided raids against the four provinces of Yu, Xu, Si, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 遣偽荊州刺史薛真度、尚書郗祁阿婆出南陽，向沙堨，築壘開溝，為南陽太守房伯玉、新野太守劉思忌所破。

translations.literal: He sent the pseudo Governor of Jing Province Xue Zhendu and the Director Xi Qi'a'po out from Nanyang toward Shapo, building ramparts and digging ditches — they were defeated by Fang Yuyu, Administrator of Nanyang, and Liu Siji, Administrator of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the pseudo Governor of Jing Province Xue Zhendu and Director Xi Qi'a'po out from Nanyang toward Shapo, where they built fortifications and dug trenches; Fang Yuyu, Administrator of Nanyang, and Liu Siji, Administrator of Xinye, defeated them.

sentences.zh: 春，高宗遣鎮南將軍王廣之出司州，右僕射沈文季出豫州，左衞將軍崔慧景出徐州。

translations.literal: In spring, Emperor Ming sent General Who Guards the South Wang Guangzhi out from Si Province, Right Vice Director Shen Wenji out from Yu Province, and Captain of the Left Guard Cui Huijing out from Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In spring Emperor Ming sent General Who Guards the South Wang Guangzhi out from Si Province, Right Vice Director Shen Wenji out from Yu Province, and Captain of the Left Guard Cui Huijing out from Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 宏自率眾至壽陽，軍中有黑氈行殿，容二十人坐，輦邊皆三郎曷剌真，槊多白真毦，鐵騎為羣，前後相接。

translations.literal: Hong personally led his force to Shouyang. In the army was a travelling hall of black felt large enough for twenty to sit; beside the imperial carriage were all "Three Rank Halazhen," spears mostly with white yak-hair tufts, iron cavalry massed in groups one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Hong personally led his army to Shouyang. The camp included a black felt travelling hall seating twenty men; beside the imperial carriage stood Three-Rank Halazhen guards, spears mostly tipped with white yak-hair tufts, and iron cavalry massed in continuous ranks.

sentences.zh: 步軍皆烏楯槊，綴接以黑蝦蟆幡。

translations.literal: The infantry all carried black-shield spears, linked together with black toad banners.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry all bore black-shield spears, arrayed in linked formation behind black toad banners.

sentences.zh: 牛車及驢駱駞載軍資妓女，三十許萬人。

translations.literal: Ox carts and donkeys, camels laden with military supplies and camp women — some three hundred thousand people in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ox carts, donkeys, and camels carried military supplies and camp followers — some three hundred thousand people in all.

sentences.zh: 不攻城，登八公山，賦詩而去。

translations.literal: He did not assault the city; he climbed Mount Bagong, composed a poem, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He did not besiege the city; instead he ascended Mount Bagong, composed a poem, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 別圍鍾離城，徐州刺史蕭惠休、輔國將軍申希祖拒守，出兵奮擊，宏眾敗，多赴淮死。

translations.literal: Separately he besieged Zhongli city. Xiao Huixiu, Governor of Xu Province, and Shen Xizu, General Who Assists the State, held the defense; sallying forth in fierce attack they defeated Hong's army, many of whom drowned in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Separately he besieged Zhongli. Xiao Huixiu, Governor of Xu Province, and Shen Xizu, General Who Assists the State, defended the city; sallying forth in fierce counterattack they routed Hong's army, many of whom drowned in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 乃分軍據邵陽州，柵斷水路，夾築二城。

translations.literal: He then divided his army to hold Shaoyang Province, palisading the waterways and building two cities on either side.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his forces to hold Shaoyang Province, blocking the waterways with palisades and building two cities on either flank.

sentences.zh: 右衞將軍蕭坦之遣軍主裴叔業攻二城，拔之。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi, Captain of the Right Guard, sent Commander Pei Shuye to assault the two cities and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi, Captain of the Right Guard, sent Commander Pei Shuye to attack the two cities and captured them.

sentences.zh: 惠休又募人出燒虜攻城車，虜力竭不能剋。

translations.literal: Huixiu also recruited men to sally forth and burn the siege engines of the barbarians; the barbarians exhausted their strength and could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huixiu also recruited men to sally out and burn the barbarians' siege engines; the barbarians exhausted their strength and could not capture the city.

sentences.zh: 王奐之誅，子肅奔虜，宏以為鎮南將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Huanzhi was executed, his son Su fled to the Northern Wei; Hong appointed him General Who Guards the South and Governor of Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Huanzhi was executed, his son Su fled to the Northern Wei; Hong appointed him General Who Guards the South and Governor of Southern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 遣肅與劉昶號二十萬眾，圍義陽。

translations.literal: He sent Su with Liu Chang — their combined force numbering two hundred thousand — to besiege Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Su together with Liu Chang — their combined force said to number two hundred thousand — to besiege Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史蕭誕拒戰，虜築圍壍柵三重，燒居民淨盡，并力攻城，城中負楯而立。

translations.literal: Xiao Dan, Governor of Si Province, resisted in battle. The barbarians built three rings of trenches and palisades, burned the residents clean away, and concentrated their strength on the assault; within the city the defenders stood shielded against the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Dan, Governor of Si Province, resisted in battle. The barbarians built three rings of trenches and palisades, burned the surrounding settlements to the ground, and concentrated all their strength on the assault; inside the city the defenders stood behind their shields.

sentences.zh: 王廣之都督救援，虜遣三萬餘人逆攻太子右率蕭季敞於下梁，季敞戰不利。

translations.literal: Wang Guangzhi as commander came to the rescue. The barbarians sent more than thirty thousand men to intercept and attack Xiao Jichang, Captain of the Right for the Crown Prince, at Xialiang; Jichang fared poorly in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi came as overall commander to relieve the city. The barbarians sent more than thirty thousand men to intercept Crown Prince's Captain of the Right Xiao Jichang at Xialiang; Jichang fought poorly.

sentences.zh: 司州城內告急，王廣之遣軍主黃門侍郎梁王閒道先進，與太子右率蕭誄、輔國將軍徐玄慶、荊州軍主魯休烈據賢首山，出虜不備。

translations.literal: With the city of Si Province in urgent distress, Wang Guangzhi sent Commander Liang Wang by a hidden route to advance first, joining Xiao Shuo, Captain of the Right for the Crown Prince, Xu Xuanqing, General Who Assists the State, and Lu Xiulie, commander of Jing Province forces, to seize Mount Xianshou — taking the barbarians unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: With Si Province's capital in urgent peril, Wang Guangzhi sent Commander Liang Wang by a hidden route to advance first, joining Crown Prince's Captain of the Right Xiao Shuo, General Who Assists the State Xu Xuanqing, and Jing Province commander Lu Xiulie to seize Mount Xianshou and take the barbarians by surprise.

sentences.zh: 城內見援軍至，蕭誕遣長史王伯瑜及軍主崔恭祖出攻虜柵，因風放火，梁王等眾軍自外擊之，昶、肅棄圍引退，追擊破之。

translations.literal: When the relief army arrived, those within the city saw them; Xiao Dan sent Chief Administrator Wang Boyu and Commander Cui Gongzu to sally forth and attack the barbarian palisades. They set fire with the wind, and Liang Wang and the other armies struck from outside; Liu Chang and Su abandoned the siege and withdrew; the pursuers broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the relief force arrive, Xiao Dan sent Chief Administrator Wang Boyu and Commander Cui Gongzu to sally out and attack the barbarian palisades. They set fire with the wind while Liang Wang and the other armies struck from without; Liu Chang and Su abandoned the siege and withdrew, and the pursuers routed them.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍桓和出西陰平，偽魯郡公郯城戍主帶莫樓、為東海太守江道僧設伏路側，和與合戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Huan He, General Who Assists the State, marched out from Western Yinping. The pseudo Duke of Lu, garrison commander of Tancheng Dai Molou, and Jiang Daoseng, Administrator of Donghai, set an ambush by the road; He joined battle with them and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan He, General Who Assists the State, marched out from Western Yinping. The pseudo Duke of Lu, Tancheng garrison commander Dai Molou, and Jiang Daoseng, Administrator of Donghai, set an ambush along the road; He joined battle and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 青、徐民降者百餘家。

translations.literal: Families from Qing and Xu who surrendered numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred families from Qing and Xu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 青、冀二州刺史王洪範遣軍主崔延攻虜紀城，竝拔之。

translations.literal: Wang Hongfan, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, sent Commander Cui Yan to attack the barbarian-held city of Ji — both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongfan, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, sent Commander Cui Yan to attack the barbarian-held city of Ji and captured it.

sentences.zh: 宏先又遣偽尚書盧陽烏、華州刺史韋靈智攻赭陽城，北襄城太守成公期拒守。

translations.literal: Earlier Hong had also sent the pseudo Director Lu Yangwu and Wei Lingzhi, Governor of Hua Province, to attack the city of Zheyang; Cheng Gongqi, Administrator of Northern Xiangcheng, held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hong had also sent the pseudo Director Lu Yangwu and Hua Province Governor Wei Lingzhi to attack Zheyang; Cheng Gongqi, Administrator of Northern Xiangcheng, held the city in defense.

sentences.zh: 虜攻城百餘日，設以鉤衝，不捨晝夜，期所殺傷數千人。

translations.literal: The barbarians besieged the city for more than a hundred days, deploying hook-rams without ceasing day or night; Gongqi's side killed and wounded several thousand of them.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians besieged the city for more than a hundred days, deploying hook-rams without pause day or night; Gongqi's defenders killed and wounded several thousand of them.

sentences.zh: 臺又遣軍主垣歷生、蔡道貴救援，陽烏等退，官軍追擊破之。

translations.literal: The court also sent Commanders Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogui to the rescue; Yangwu and the others withdrew, and the government troops pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent Commanders Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogui to relieve the city; Yangwu and the others withdrew, and the imperial army pursued and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 夏，虜又攻司州櫟城二戍，戍主魏僧岷、朱僧起拒敗之。

translations.literal: In summer the barbarians again attacked the two garrisons of Licheng in Si Province; garrison commanders Wei Sengmin and Zhu Sengqi repulsed and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the barbarians again attacked the two garrisons at Licheng in Si Province; garrison commanders Wei Sengmin and Zhu Sengqi repulsed and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 偽安南將軍、梁州刺史魏郡王元英十萬餘人通斜谷，寇南鄭。

translations.literal: The pseudo General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Liang Province, Prince of Wei Commandery Yuan Ying, with more than a hundred thousand men passed through Xiegou and raided Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The pseudo General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Liang Province, Prince of Wei Commandery Yuan Ying, with more than a hundred thousand men passed through Xiegou and raided Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史蕭懿遣軍主姜山安、趙超宗等數軍萬餘人，分據角弩、白馬、沮水拒戰，大敗。

translations.literal: Xiao Yi, Governor of Liang Province, sent Commanders Jiang Shan'an, Zhao Chaozong, and others — several armies totaling more than ten thousand — to hold positions at Jiaonu, Baima, and Jushui and resist; they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi, Governor of Liang Province, sent Commanders Jiang Shan'an, Zhao Chaozong, and others — several armies totaling more than ten thousand men — to hold Jiaonu, Baima, and Jushui and resist; they were utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 英進圍南鄭，土山衝車，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Ying advanced to besiege Nanzheng, raising earth mounds and deploying battering rams without rest day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Ying advanced to besiege Nanzheng, building earth mounds and deploying battering rams without cease day or night.

sentences.zh: 懿率東從兵二千餘人固守拒戰，隨手摧卻。

translations.literal: Yi led his eastern followers, more than two thousand men, to hold firm and resist; as each assault came he beat it back.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led his eastern followers, more than two thousand men, to hold the city and resist; whenever the enemy attacked he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 英攻城自春至夏六十餘日不下，死傷甚眾，軍中糧盡，擣麴為食，畜菜葉直千錢。

translations.literal: Ying besieged the city from spring to summer for more than sixty days without taking it; casualties were extremely heavy; army provisions ran out — they pounded grain stalks for food; stored vegetable leaves sold for a thousand cash apiece.
translations.idiomatic: Ying besieged the city from spring through summer for more than sixty days without capturing it; casualties were extremely heavy, provisions ran out, and the army pounded grain stalks for food while stored vegetable leaves fetched a thousand cash apiece.

sentences.zh: 懿先遣軍主韓嵩等征獠，回軍援州城，至黃牛川，為虜所破。

translations.literal: Yi had earlier sent Commander Han Song and others to campaign against the Liao; they returned to relieve the provincial capital but at Huangniu Stream were defeated by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had earlier sent Commander Han Song and others to campaign against the Liao; they turned back to relieve the provincial capital but were defeated by the barbarians at Huangniu Stream.

sentences.zh: 懿遣氐人楊元秀還仇池，說氐起兵斷虜運道，氐即舉眾攻破虜歷城、睪蘭、駱谷、仇池、平洛、蘇勒六戍。

translations.literal: Yi sent the Di tribesman Yang Yuanxiu back to Chouci to persuade the Di to rise and cut the barbarians' supply lines; the Di immediately mustered and captured the six garrisons of Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Chouci, Pingluo, and Sule held by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent the Di tribesman Yang Yuanxiu back to Chouci to persuade the Di to rise and cut the barbarians' supply lines; the Di immediately mustered and captured the six barbarian garrisons at Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Chouci, Pingluo, and Sule.

sentences.zh: 偽尚書北梁州刺史辛黑末戰死。

translations.literal: The pseudo Director and Governor of Northern Liang Province Xin Heimo was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The pseudo Director and Governor of Northern Liang Province Xin Heimo was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 英遣軍副仇池公楊靈珍據泥公山，武興城主楊集始遣弟集朗與歸國氐楊馥之及義軍主徐曜甫迎戰於黃亘，大敗奔歸。

translations.literal: Ying sent Army Vice-Commander Lord of Chouci Yang Lingzhen to hold Nigong Mountain; Wuxing City Commander Yang Jishi sent his younger brother Jilang together with the returned-country Di Yang Fuzhi and Righteous Army Commander Xu Yaofu to meet them in battle at Huanggen — they suffered a great defeat and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Ying sent Army Vice-Commander Lord of Chouci Yang Lingzhen to hold Nigong Mountain. Wuxing City Commander Yang Jishi sent his younger brother Jilang, together with the returned-country Di Yang Fuzhi and Righteous Army Commander Xu Yaofu, to meet them in battle at Huanggen; they were routed and fled back.

sentences.zh: 時梁州土豪范凝、梁季羣於家請英設會，伏兵欲殺英，事覺，英執季羣殺之，凝竄走。

translations.literal: At the time, Liang Province local strongmen Fan Ning and Liang Jiqun invited Ying to a feast at their home and set an ambush intending to kill Ying; the plot was discovered — Ying seized Jiqun and executed him, while Ning fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Liang Province local magnates Fan Ning and Liang Jiqun invited Ying to a feast at home and lay in ambush to kill him; when the plot was discovered Ying seized Jiqun and put him to death, while Ning fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 英退保濁水，聞氐眾盛，與楊靈珍復俱退入斜谷，會天大雨，軍馬含漬，截竹煮米，於馬上持炬炊而食。

translations.literal: Ying withdrew to hold at Zhuoshui; hearing that Di forces were numerous, he and Yang Lingzhen again retreated together into Xiegu; it happened to pour with rain — horses and troops were soaked through; they cut bamboo to cook rice, holding torches on horseback to cook and eat.
translations.idiomatic: Ying withdrew to defend Zhuoshui; hearing that Di forces were strong, he and Yang Lingzhen retreated together into Xiegu. Heavy rain soaked horses and men alike; they cut bamboo to cook rice and ate on horseback, torches in hand.

sentences.zh: 英至下辨，靈珍弟婆羅阿卜珍反，襲擊，英眾散，射中英頰。

translations.literal: When Ying reached Xiabian, Lingzhen's younger brother Poluo Abu Zhen rebelled and launched a surprise attack; Ying's troops scattered, and an arrow struck Ying in the cheek.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying reached Xiabian, Lingzhen's younger brother Poluo Abu Zhen rebelled and attacked; Ying's troops scattered and an arrow struck him in the cheek.

sentences.zh: 偽陵江將軍悅楊生領鐵騎死戰救之，得免。

translations.literal: The pseudo Lingjiang General Yue Yangsheng led iron cavalry in a death struggle to rescue him, and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The pseudo Lingjiang General Yue Yangsheng led armored cavalry in a desperate fight to save him, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 梁、漢平。

translations.literal: Liang and Han were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Han were pacified.

sentences.zh: 武都太守杜靈瑗、奮武將軍望法憘、寧朔將軍望法泰、州治中皇甫耽竝拒虜戰死。

translations.literal: Wudu Prefect Du Lingyuan, Fierce-Warrior General Wang Faxi, Pacifying-North General Wang Fatai, and Provincial Senior Clerk Huangfu Dan all resisted the barbarians and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wudu Prefect Du Lingyuan, Fierce-Warrior General Wang Faxi, Pacifying-North General Wang Fatai, and Provincial Senior Clerk Huangfu Dan all resisted the barbarians and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 追贈靈瑗、法憘羽林監，法泰積射將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Lingyuan and Faxi as Supervisors of the Feathered Forest Guard; Fatai as Accumulative-Shooting General.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyuan and Faxi were posthumously enfeoffed as Supervisors of the Feathered Forest Guard, and Fatai as Accumulative-Shooting General.

sentences.zh: 時偽洛州刺史賈異寇甲口，為上洛太守李靜所破。

translations.literal: At the time the pseudo Governor of Luozhou Jia Yi raided Jiakou and was defeated by Shangluo Prefect Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the pseudo Governor of Luozhou Jia Yi raided Jiakou and was routed by Shangluo Prefect Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 三年，虜又攻司州櫟城，為戍主魏僧岷所拒破。

translations.literal: In the third year the barbarians again attacked Lik City in Sizhou and were repulsed and defeated by Garrison Commander Wei Songmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the barbarians again attacked Lik City in Sizhou and were beaten back by Garrison Commander Wei Songmin.

sentences.zh: 秋，虜遣軍襲漣口，東海太守鄭延祉棄西城走，東城猶固守，臺遣冠軍將軍兖州刺史徐玄慶救援，虜引退，延祉伏罪。

translations.literal: In autumn the barbarians sent troops to raid Lian Estuary; Donghai Prefect Zheng Yanzhi abandoned the west city and fled, while the east city still held firm; the Court sent Champion General and Yanzhou Inspector Xu Xuanqing to the rescue; the barbarians withdrew, and Yanzhi submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the barbarians raided Lian Estuary. Donghai Prefect Zheng Yanzhi abandoned the west city and fled while the east city continued to hold. The Court sent Champion General and Yanzhou Inspector Xu Xuanqing to relieve the siege; the barbarians withdrew and Yanzhi submitted to punishment.

sentences.zh: 初，偽太后馮氏兄昌黎王馮莎二女，大馮美而有疾，為尼，小馮為宏皇后，生偽太子詢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Dowager Feng's brother the Prince of Changli Feng Sha had two daughters: the elder Feng was beautiful but sickly and became a nun; the younger Feng was Hong's empress and bore the pseudo crown prince Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Dowager Feng's brother, Prince of Changli Feng Sha, had two daughters. The elder Feng was beautiful but afflicted with illness and became a nun; the younger Feng was Hong's empress and bore the pseudo crown prince Xun.

sentences.zh: 後大馮疾差，宏納為昭儀。

translations.literal: Later when the elder Feng's illness had abated, Hong took her in as Worthy Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the elder Feng recovered from her illness, Hong took her in as Worthy Lady.

sentences.zh: 宏初徙都，詢意不樂，思歸桑乾。

translations.literal: When Hong first moved the capital, Xun was displeased in spirit and longed to return to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong first moved the capital, Xun was unhappy and longed to return to Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 宏制衣冠與之，詢竊毀裂，解髮為編服左衽。

translations.literal: Hong had court dress made for him; Xun secretly tore and destroyed it, let down his hair, and wore braided barbarian dress with the left lapel.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had court robes made for him; Xun secretly ripped them apart, wore his hair loose, and dressed in braided nomad garb with the left lapel forward.

sentences.zh: 大馮有寵，日夜讒詢。

translations.literal: The elder Feng had Hong's favor and slandered Xun day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The elder Feng held Hong's favor and slandered Xun day and night.

sentences.zh: 宏出鄴城馬射，詢因是欲叛北歸，密選宮中御馬三千疋置河陰渚。

translations.literal: When Hong went out from Ye for mounted archery, Xun took the opportunity to plan rebellion and flight north; secretly he selected three thousand imperial horses from the palace and stationed them on the south bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong went out from Ye for mounted archery, Xun seized the chance to plot rebellion and flight north, secretly choosing three thousand palace horses and stationing them on the south bank of the river.

sentences.zh: 皇后聞之，召執詢，馳使告宏，宏徙詢無鼻城，在河橋北二里，尋殺之，以庶人禮葬。

translations.literal: The empress heard of it, summoned and seized Xun, and sent a courier galloping to inform Hong; Hong relocated Xun to Wubi City, two li north of He Bridge — soon he was killed and buried with commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: The empress learned of it, had Xun seized, and sent a fast courier to Hong; Hong exiled Xun to Wubi City, two li north of He Bridge, soon had him killed, and buried him with the rites due a commoner.

sentences.zh: 立大馮為皇后，便立偽太子恪，是歲，偽也。

translations.literal: The elder Feng was installed as empress, and the pseudo crown prince Ke was immediately installed — that year the pseudo reign title was altered.
translations.idiomatic: The elder Feng was installed as empress, and the pseudo crown prince Ke was immediately established; that year they altered the reign title.

sentences.zh: 偽征北將軍恒州刺史鉅鹿公伏鹿孤賀鹿渾守桑乾，宏從叔平陽王安壽戍懷柵，在桑乾西北。

translations.literal: The pseudo North-Conquering General and Hengzhou Inspector Duke of Julu Fulu Gu Heluhun held Sanggan; Hong's cousin Prince of Pingyang An Shou garrisoned the Huai palisade northwest of Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: The pseudo North-Conquering General and Hengzhou Inspector Duke of Julu Fulu Gu Heluhun held Sanggan, while Hong's cousin Prince of Pingyang An Shou garrisoned the Huai palisade northwest of Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 渾非宏任用中國人，與偽定州刺史馮翊公目隣、安樂公托跋阿幹兒謀立安壽，分據河北。

translations.literal: Heluhun resented that Hong employed Chinese men; together with the pseudo Dingzhou Inspector Duke of Fengyi Mu Lin and Duke of Anle Tuoba A'gan'er he plotted to install An Shou and divide and hold the lands north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Heluhun resented Hong's reliance on Chinese officials; with the pseudo Dingzhou Inspector Duke of Fengyi Mu Lin and Duke of Anle Tuoba A'gan'er he plotted to install An Shou and carve up the lands north of the River.

sentences.zh: 期久不遂，安壽懼，告宏。

translations.literal: The appointed day long went unfulfilled; An Shou grew afraid and informed Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When the long-delayed plot failed to come off, An Shou feared exposure and reported to Hong.

sentences.zh: 殺渾等數百人，任安壽如故。

translations.literal: [Hong] killed Heluhun and several hundred others; An Shou's appointment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hong killed Heluhun and several hundred others, but left An Shou in his post as before.

sentences.zh: 先是偽荊州刺史薛真度、尚書郄祁阿婆為房伯玉所破，宏怒，以南陽小郡，誓取滅之。

translations.literal: Earlier the pseudo Jingzhou Inspector Xue Zhendu and Director Qiqi Apo had been defeated by Fang Boyu; Hong was enraged — for a petty southern commandery like Nanyang, he vowed to exterminate it utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the pseudo Jingzhou Inspector Xue Zhendu and Director Qiqi Apo had been defeated by Fang Boyu. Hong flew into a rage — over a mere southern commandery like Nanyang he swore total destruction.

sentences.zh: 四年，自率軍向雍州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he personally led an army toward Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he personally led an army toward Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 宏先至南陽，房伯玉嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Hong reached Nanyang first; Fang Boyu closed the city and refused to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Hong reached Nanyang first; Fang Boyu barred the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 宏從數萬騎，罩黃繖，去城一里。

translations.literal: Hong followed with tens of thousands of horsemen, shaded by a yellow imperial parasol, one li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hong followed with tens of thousands of horsemen beneath a yellow imperial parasol, halting one li from the city.

sentences.zh: 遣偽中書舍人公孫雲謂伯玉曰：「我今蕩一六合，與先

translations.literal: He sent the pseudo Palace Secretariat Attendant Gongsun Yun to say to Boyu: "I shall now sweep clean all within the four seas and six directions, differing from my predecessors
translations.idiomatic: He sent the pseudo Palace Secretariat Attendant Gongsun Yun to address Boyu: "I mean now to sweep all within the four seas, and my conduct differs from that of my predecessors

translations.literal: after
translations.idiomatic: after

sentences.zh: 行異。

translations.literal: — conduct differs.
translations.idiomatic: — my ways differ.

sentences.zh: 先行冬去春還，不為停久；

translations.literal: Earlier campaigns went out in winter and returned in spring, not staying long;
translations.idiomatic: Previous emperors marched out in winter and returned in spring, never tarrying long;

sentences.zh: 今誓不有所剋，終不還北，停此或三五年。

translations.literal: Now I vow that unless I achieve conquest I will never return north — I may linger here three or five years.
translations.idiomatic: Now I swear that unless I conquer I shall never return north; I may remain here three or even five years.

sentences.zh: 卿此城是我六龍之首，無容不先攻取。

translations.literal: Your city is the head of my six dragons — it cannot go without being attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: Your city is the foremost target of my six dragon-banners — it must be taken first.

sentences.zh: 遠一年，中不過百日，近不過一月，非為難殄。

translations.literal: At farthest a year, at most a hundred days at middle distance, at nearest no more than a month — it is not hard to exterminate.
translations.idiomatic: At most a year; at middle distance no more than a hundred days; at nearest less than a month — hardly difficult to destroy.

sentences.zh: 若不改迷，當斬卿首，梟之軍門。

translations.literal: If you do not abandon your delusion, I shall cut off your head and display it before the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not repent, I shall take your head and display it before the army gate.

sentences.zh: 闔城無貳，幸可改禍為福。

translations.literal: The whole city harbors no split loyalty — you may yet turn calamity to blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the whole city can turn disaster to fortune — there must be no divided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 但卿有三罪，今令卿知。

translations.literal: Yet you bear three crimes — I now let you know them.
translations.idiomatic: You have committed three crimes, and I shall name them.

sentences.zh: 卿先事武帝，蒙在左右，不能盡節前主，而盡節今主，此是一罪。

translations.literal: You first served Emperor Wu and enjoyed his close favor, yet failed to give full loyalty to your former lord while giving full loyalty to your present lord — this is the first crime.
translations.idiomatic: You once served Emperor Wu at his side, yet you did not die for your former lord while you now die for your present one — that is your first crime.

sentences.zh: 前歲遣偏師薛真度暫來此，卿遂破傷，此是二罪。

translations.literal: Last year I sent a detached force under Xue Zhendu briefly here; you wounded and defeated them — this is the second crime.
translations.idiomatic: Last year I sent Xue Zhendu here at the head of a detached force; you routed and wounded him — that is your second crime.

sentences.zh: 武帝之胤悉被誅戮，初無報効，而反為今主盡節，違天害理，此是三罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's descendants were all executed; you rendered no repayment of the debt, yet instead give full loyalty to your present lord — contravening Heaven and violating principle — this is the third crime.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's line was wiped out, yet you owed them nothing and now die for another master — defying Heaven and reason — that is your third crime.

sentences.zh: 不可容恕。

translations.literal: This cannot be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 聽卿三思，勿令闔城受苦。」

translations.literal: I allow you three times to think — do not let the whole city suffer."
translations.idiomatic: Think carefully — do not bring suffering upon the whole city.

sentences.zh: 伯玉遣軍副樂稚柔答曰：「承欲見攻圍，期於必剋，卑微常人，得抗大威，真可謂獲其死所。

translations.literal: Boyu sent Army Vice-Commander Yue Zhirou to reply: "Learning that you wish to besiege and assault us, bent on certain victory — a humble common man like me, able to resist your great majesty — one may truly call this finding the place where I shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu sent Army Vice-Commander Yue Zhirou to reply: "Hearing that you mean to besiege us and must prevail — a humble man like me, able to resist your great majesty — I may truly call this finding the place where I shall die.

sentences.zh: 先蒙武帝

translations.literal: I first received Emperor Wu's
translations.idiomatic: I first received Emperor Wu's

translations.literal: special
translations.idiomatic: special

sentences.zh: 採〔拔〕，賜預左右，犬馬知恩，寧容無感。

translations.literal: selection and promotion, granted a place at his side — even a dog or horse knows gratitude; could I be without feeling?
translations.idiomatic: selection and promotion, granted a place at his side — even a dog or horse knows gratitude; could I be without feeling?

sentences.zh: 但隆昌延興，昏悖違常，聖明纂業，家國不殊。

translations.literal: But the Longchang and Yanxing reigns were benighted and perverse, straying from the norm; the sage and enlightened one succeeded to the enterprise — family and state are not different.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Longchang and Yanxing reigns were corrupt and lawless; the wise sovereign succeeded to the throne — family and realm are one.

sentences.zh: 此則進不負心，退不愧幽。

translations.literal: Thus advancing I betray no loyalty in my heart; retreating I need not feel shame before the shades.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing I betray no one's trust; retreating I need feel no shame before the dead.

sentences.zh: 前歲薛真度導誘邊氓，遂見陵突，既荷國恩，聊耳撲掃。

translations.literal: Last year Xue Zhendu led and enticed our border people; we were therefore subjected to insult and assault — having borne the state's grace, I merely swept them aside as one might brush cobwebs.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Xue Zhendu incited our border folk and we drove him off — having received the state's grace, I did no more than brush him aside.

sentences.zh: 回己而言，應略此責。」

translations.literal: Turning to myself, this charge should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, that charge should be set aside.

sentences.zh: 宏引軍向城南寺前頓止，從東南角溝橋上過，伯玉先遣勇士數人著斑衣虎頭帽，從伏竇下忽出，宏人馬驚退，殺數人，宏呼善射將原靈度射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Hong led his army to halt before the temple south of the city; crossing by the ditch bridge at the southeast corner, Boyu had first sent several braves in spotted garments and tiger-head caps to burst suddenly from hidden tunnels beneath — Hong's men and horses startled and fell back; several were killed. Hong called the fine archer General Yuan Lingdu to shoot them; they fell as the bowstrings sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Hong halted his army before the south-city temple and crossed via the ditch bridge at the southeast corner. Boyu had sent several warriors in spotted robes and tiger-head caps to burst from hidden tunnels below; Hong's men panicked and retreated, and several were killed. Hong summoned the archer General Yuan Lingdu, who felled them as each bowstring sang.

sentences.zh: 宏乃過。

translations.literal: Hong then crossed over.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then crossed.

sentences.zh: 宏時大舉南寇，偽咸陽王元憘、彭城王元勰、常侍王元嵩、寶掌王元麗、廣陵侯元燮、都督大將軍劉昶、王肅、楊大眼、奚康生、長孫稚等三十六軍，前後相繼，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: Hong was then conducting a major southern invasion — the pseudo Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi, Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, Regular Attendant Yuan Song, Prince of Baozhang Yuan Li, Marquis of Guangling Yuan Xie, Grand Generals-in-Chief Liu Chang, Wang Su, Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, Zhangsun Zhi, and thirty-six armies in all came one after another; the host was proclaimed at a million.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then launched a great southern campaign. The pseudo Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi, Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, Regular Attendant Yuan Song, Prince of Baozhang Yuan Li, Marquis of Guangling Yuan Xie, and Grand Generals-in-Chief Liu Chang, Wang Su, Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and Zhangsun Zhi led thirty-six armies in succession; the host was said to number a million.

sentences.zh: 其諸王軍朱色鼓，公侯綠色鼓，伯子男黑色鼓，竝有鼙角，吹脣沸地。

translations.literal: Among them the princes' armies used vermilion drums; dukes and marquises green drums; viscounts, barons, and lesser nobles black drums — all had war drums and horns whose blasts made the earth thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' hosts carried vermilion drums; dukes and marquises green drums; viscounts, barons, and lesser nobles black drums — war drums and horns together made the earth shake.

sentences.zh: 宏留偽咸陽王憘圍南陽，進向新野，新野太守劉思忌亦拒守。

translations.literal: Hong left the pseudo Prince of Xianyang Xi to besiege Nanyang and advanced toward Xinye; Xinye Prefect Liu Siji likewise closed the city and held.
translations.idiomatic: Hong left the pseudo Prince of Xianyang Xi to besiege Nanyang and marched on Xinye, where Prefect Liu Siji also barred the gates and defended.

sentences.zh: 臺先遣軍主直閤將軍胡松助北襄城太守成公期守赭陽城，軍主鮑舉助西汝南、北義陽二郡太守黃瑤起戍舞陰城。

translations.literal: The Court had first sent Commanders Direct-Gate General Hu Song to aid Beixiangcheng Prefect Cheng Gongqi in holding Zheyang City, and Commander Bao Ju to aid the Prefect of West Runan and North Yiyang commanderies Huang Yaoqi in garrisoning Wuyin City.
translations.idiomatic: The Court had already sent Commander Direct-Gate General Hu Song to help Beixiangcheng Prefect Cheng Gongqi hold Zheyang, and Commander Bao Ju to help Huang Yaoqi, Prefect of West Runan and North Yiyang, garrison Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 宏攻圍新野城，戰鬪不息。

translations.literal: Hong besieged Xinye City; fighting did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Hong besieged Xinye and fighting raged without pause.

sentences.zh: 遣人謂城中曰：「房伯玉已降，汝南

translations.literal: He sent men to say to the city: "Fang Boyu has already surrendered; Runan
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to address the city: "Fang Boyu has already surrendered; Runan

translations.literal: why
translations.idiomatic: why

sentences.zh: 〔何〕獨自取糜碎？」

translations.literal: why must you alone seek your own destruction?
translations.idiomatic: why must you alone seek your own destruction?

sentences.zh: 思忌令人對曰：「城中兵食猶多，未暇從汝小虜語也。」

translations.literal: Siji had someone reply: "Provisions and troops in the city remain plentiful; we have no leisure to heed the words of you little barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Siji sent a reply: "The city still has ample troops and grain — we have no time for talk with you barbarian whelps.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史曹虎遣軍至均口，不進。

translations.literal: Yong Province Inspector Cao Hu sent troops to Jun Estuary but did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province Inspector Cao Hu sent troops to Jun Estuary but halted without advancing.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，城陷，縛思忌，問之曰：「今欲降未？」

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai the city fell; [Hong] bound Siji and asked him: "Do you wish to surrender now?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai the city fell; Hong bound Siji and asked: "Do you wish to surrender now?

sentences.zh: 思忌曰：「寧為南鬼，不為北臣。」

translations.literal: Siji said: "Better to be a southern ghost than a northern subject."
translations.idiomatic: Siji answered: "I would rather be a ghost in the south than a subject in the north.

sentences.zh: 乃死。

translations.literal: Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 贈冠軍將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Champion General and Liang Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed Champion General and Liang Province Inspector.

sentences.zh: 於是沔北大震，湖陽戍主蔡道福、赭陽城主成公期及軍主胡松、舞陰城主黃瑤起及軍主鮑舉、從陽太守席謙竝棄城走。

translations.literal: Thereupon north of the Mian there was great panic — Husyang Garrison Commander Cai Daofu, Zheyang City Commander Cheng Gongqi and Commander Hu Song, Wuyin City Commander Huang Yaoqi and Commander Bao Ju, and Congyang Prefect Xi Qian all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread north of the Mian. Husyang Garrison Commander Cai Daofu, Zheyang Commander Cheng Gongqi, Commander Hu Song, Wuyin Commander Huang Yaoqi, Commander Bao Ju, and Congyang Prefect Xi Qian all abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 虜追軍獲瑤起，王肅募人臠食其肉。

translations.literal: The barbarians' pursuit force captured Yaoqi; Wang Su recruited men to carve his flesh and eat it.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian pursuit captured Yaoqi; Wang Su paid men to carve up his flesh and eat it.

sentences.zh: 追贈冠軍將軍、兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Champion General and Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqi was posthumously enfeoffed Champion General and Yanzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 數日，房伯玉以城降。

translations.literal: Several days later Fang Boyu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Fang Boyu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 伯玉，清河人。

translations.literal: Boyu was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 既降，虜以為龍驤將軍，伯玉不肯受。

translations.literal: After surrendering, the barbarians wished to appoint him Dragon-Steed General; Boyu refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: After his surrender the barbarians offered him the title Dragon-Steed General; Boyu refused.

sentences.zh: 高宗知其志，月給其子希哲錢五千，米二十斛。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong knew his resolve and each month granted his son Xizhe five thousand cash and twenty hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong understood his loyalty and each month sent his son Xizhe five thousand cash and twenty hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 後伯玉就虜求南邊一郡，為馮翊太守，生子幼，便教其騎馬，常欲南歸。

translations.literal: Later Boyu asked the barbarians for a southern commandery and became Fengyi Prefect; his son was still young, yet he taught him to ride — he always wished to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Later Boyu asked the barbarians for a post on the southern frontier and became Fengyi Prefect; though his son was still young he taught him horsemanship, always longing to return south.

sentences.zh: 永元末，希哲入虜，伯玉大怒曰：「我力屈至此，不能死節，猶望汝在本朝以報國恩。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, Xizhe entered barbarian territory; Boyu raged and said: "My strength has bent to this point — unable to die in loyalty — yet I still hoped you would remain in our court to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongyuan, Xizhe entered barbarian territory; Boyu raged and said: "My strength has bent to this point — unable to die in loyalty — yet I still hoped you would remain in our court to repay the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 我若從心，亦欲間關求反。

translations.literal: Had I followed my heart, I too would have wished to make my way through hardship seeking return.
translations.idiomatic: Had I followed my own heart, I too would have braved every pass to flee back.

sentences.zh: 汝何為失計？」

translations.literal: Why have you lost your judgment?"
translations.idiomatic: Why have you lost your wits?

sentences.zh: 遂卒虜中。

translations.literal: He thereafter died in barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after in barbarian territory.

sentences.zh: 虜得沔北五郡。

translations.literal: The barbarians obtained five commanderies north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians took five commanderies north of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 宏自將二十萬騎破太子率崔慧景等於鄧城，進至樊城，臨沔水而去。

translations.literal: Hong personally led two hundred thousand horsemen to defeat the crown prince leading Cui Huijing and others at Deng City; he advanced to Fancheng, came to the Mian River, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hong personally led two hundred thousand cavalry to defeat the crown prince and Cui Huijing at Deng City, advanced to Fancheng on the Mian, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 還洛陽，聞太尉陳顯達經略五郡，圍馬圈，宏復率大眾南攻，破顯達而死。

translations.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he heard that Grand Commandant Chen Xianda was managing five commanderies and besieging Maquan; Hong again led a great host south to attack, defeated Xianda, and [Xianda] died.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Luoyang he learned that Grand Commandant Chen Xianda had seized five commanderies and was besieging Maquan; Hong marched south again with a vast army, routed Xianda, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 喪還，未至洛四百餘里，稱宏詔，徵偽太子恪會魯陽。

translations.literal: As the funeral cortège returned, still more than four hundred li from Luoyang, they issued orders in Hong's name summoning the pseudo crown prince Ke to meet at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral procession returned, still over four hundred li from Luoyang, orders were issued in Hong's name summoning the pseudo crown prince Ke to Luyang.

sentences.zh: 恪至，勰以宏偽法服衣之，始發喪。

translations.literal: When Ke arrived, Xie clothed him in Hong's funeral raiment according to pseudo custom, and only then was mourning proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke arrived, Xie dressed him in Hong's mourning regalia by barbarian custom, and mourning was formally begun.

sentences.zh: 至洛，乃宣布州郡，舉哀制服，諡孝文皇帝。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, they then announced it to provinces and commanderies, raised lamentation and put on mourning dress, and gave the posthumous title Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Luoyang, they announced the death throughout the realm, raised lamentation, and invested Hong with the posthumous title Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 是年，王肅為虜制官品百司，皆如中國。

translations.literal: That year Wang Su drew up for the barbarians official grades and the hundred offices, all modeled on China.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Su established official grades and a full bureaucracy for the barbarians on the Chinese model.

sentences.zh: 凡九品，品各有二。

translations.literal: There were nine grades in all, each grade having two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: There were nine grades in all, each divided into two ranks.

sentences.zh: 肅初奔虜，自說其家被誅事狀，宏為之垂涕。

translations.literal: When Su first fled to the barbarians he recounted how his family had been executed; Hong wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su first defected he told how his family had been executed; Hong wept at the tale.

sentences.zh: 以第六妹偽彭城公主妻之。

translations.literal: [Hong] gave him his sixth younger sister, the pseudo Princess of Pengcheng, in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hong gave him his sixth sister, the pseudo Princess of Pengcheng, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 封肅平原郡公。

translations.literal: Su was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Su was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 為宅舍，以香塗壁。

translations.literal: A residence was built for him with fragrant paste smeared on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: A mansion was built for him, its walls coated with perfumed paste.

sentences.zh: 遂見信用。

translations.literal: He soon came to enjoy trust and employment.
translations.idiomatic: He soon won Hong's full trust.

sentences.zh: 恪立，號，永元二年也。

translations.literal: Ke succeeded to the throne; [reign title missing in text]; it was the second year of Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ke succeeded to the throne and altered the reign title; it was the second year of Yongyuan.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史裴叔業以壽春降虜。

translations.literal: Yuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 先是偽東徐州刺史沈陵率部曲降。

translations.literal: Earlier the pseudo East Xuzhou Inspector Shen Ling had led his personal troops in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the pseudo East Xuzhou Inspector Shen Ling had defected with his followers.

sentences.zh: 陵，吳興人，初以失志奔虜，大見任用，宏既死，故南歸，頻授徐、越二州刺史。

translations.literal: Ling was a man of Wuxing; at first, disheartened, he fled to the barbarians and was greatly employed; after Hong's death he therefore returned south and was repeatedly appointed Inspector of Xu and Yue provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was from Wuxing. He had first defected to the barbarians in frustration and rose high in their service; after Hong's death he returned south and was repeatedly made Inspector of Xu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 時王肅偽征南將軍、豫州都督。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Su was the pseudo South-Conquering General and Inspector-General of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Su held the titles pseudo South-Conquering General and Yuzhou Inspector-General.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既新失大鎮，荒人往來，詐云肅欲歸國。

translations.literal: The court having newly lost a great stronghold, frontier folk coming and going falsely reported that Su wished to return to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just lost a major stronghold, and wanderers from the frontier spread rumors that Su meant to return home.

sentences.zh: 少帝詔以肅為使持節、侍中、都督豫徐司三州、右將軍、豫州刺史，西豐公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor issued an edict appointing Su as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Inspector-General of Yu, Xu, and Si provinces, Right General, Inspector of Yuzhou, Duke of Xifeng with an estate of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor appointed Su Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Inspector-General of Yu, Xu, and Si, Right General and Inspector of Yuzhou, Duke of Xifeng with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 虜既得淮南，其夏，遣偽冠軍將軍南豫州刺史席法友攻北新蔡、安豐二郡太守胡景略於建安城，死者萬餘人，百餘日，朝廷無救，城陷，虜執景略以歸。

translations.literal: The barbarians having already taken Huainan, that summer they sent the pseudo Champion General and South Yuzhou Inspector Xi Fayou to attack Hu Jinglüe, Prefect of North Xincai and Anfeng commanderies, at Jian'an City — more than ten thousand died; after a hundred-odd days with no relief from the court the city fell, and the barbarians seized Jinglüe and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Huainan, the barbarians that summer sent the pseudo Champion General and South Yuzhou Inspector Xi Fayou to attack Jian'an, where Hu Jinglüe, Prefect of North Xincai and Anfeng, held out. More than ten thousand perished; after a hundred days without relief from the court the city fell and the barbarians carried Jinglüe away captive.

sentences.zh: 其冬，虜又遣將桓道福攻隨郡太守崔士招，破之。

translations.literal: That winter the barbarians again sent the general Huan Daofu to attack Suixiang Prefect Cui Shizhao and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the barbarians sent General Huan Daofu against Suixiang Prefect Cui Shizhao and routed him.

sentences.zh: 後偽咸陽王憘以恪年少，與氐楊集始、楊靈祐、乞佛馬居及虜大將支虎、李伯尚等十餘人，請會鴻池陂，因恪出北芒獵，襲殺之。

translations.literal: Later the false Prince of Xianyang, Xi, because Ke was young, together with the Di chieftains Yang Qishi and Yang Lingyou, Qifo Maju, and more than ten barbarian generals including Zhi Hu and Li Boshang, asked to meet at Hongchi Pond; they planned to lure Ke out to hunt on North Mang and assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Xi of Xianyang, finding Ke still young, conspired with the Di leaders Yang Qishi and Yang Lingyou, Qifo Maju, and more than ten Wei officers including Zhi Hu and Li Boshang to meet at Hongchi Pond, lure Ke to hunt on North Mang, and kill him.

sentences.zh: 憘猶豫不能發，欲更剋日。

translations.literal: Xi hesitated and could not act, wishing to fix another day.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wavered and could not strike, and wished to choose another day.

sentences.zh: 馬居說憘曰：「殿下若不至北芒，便可回師據洛城，閉四門。

translations.literal: Maju urged Xi, saying, "If Your Highness does not go to North Mang, you may turn the army back and hold Luoyang, closing the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Maju urged Xi: "If you do not go to North Mang, turn the army about, seize Luoyang, and shut the four gates.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之，必走向河北

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven hears of it, he is certain to flee north of the river
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor hears of it, he will surely flee north of the river

translations.literal: (flee)
translations.idiomatic: flee

sentences.zh: 桑乾，仍斷河橋，為河南天子。

translations.literal: to Sanggan, then cut the river bridge and become Son of Heaven south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: to Sanggan, cut the river bridge, and reign as emperor south of the river.

sentences.zh: 隔河而治，此時不可失也。」

translations.literal: Ruling across the river—this opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: To rule from south of the river—this chance must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 憘又不從。

translations.literal: Xi again would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Again Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 靈祐疑憘反己，即馳告恪。

translations.literal: Lingyou suspected Xi meant to turn against him and immediately rode to inform Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyou suspected Xi would betray him and galloped to warn Ke.

sentences.zh: 憘聞事敗，欲走渡河，而天雨暗迷道，至孝義驛，恪已得洛城。

translations.literal: Xi, hearing the affair had failed, wished to flee across the river, but rain fell and darkness confused the road; reaching Xiaoyi Post, Ke had already taken Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi learned the plot had failed, he tried to flee across the river, but rain and darkness confused the roads; at Xiaoyi Post he found Ke already held Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遣弟

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger brother

translations.literal: (Du)
translations.idiomatic: Du

sentences.zh: 〔廣〕平王領數百騎先入宮，知無變，乃還。

translations.literal: [Guang] Prince of Ping with several hundred horsemen to enter the palace first; learning there was no disturbance, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang of Ping with several hundred horsemen to enter the palace first; finding no trouble, they returned.

sentences.zh: 遣直衞三郎兵討憘，執殺之。

translations.literal: He sent the Direct Guard's third-rank soldiers to punish Xi and seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Direct Guard to seize and execute Xi.

sentences.zh: 虜法，謀反者不得葬，棄尸北芒。

translations.literal: By barbarian law, rebels might not be buried; the corpse was cast out on North Mang.
translations.idiomatic: By Wei law rebels received no burial; Xi's body was cast out on North Mang.

sentences.zh: 王肅以疾卒。

translations.literal: Wang Su died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su died of illness.

translations.literal: 【Discussion】
translations.idiomatic: 【Discussion】

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：齊、虜分，江南為國歷三代矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Qi and the barbarians were divided, and south of the Yangtze a state endured three dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: With Qi and the Wei divided, the south of the Yangtze sustained three dynasties as a realm.

sentences.zh: 華夏分崩，舊京幅裂，觀舋阻兵，事興東晉。

translations.literal: The Central Kingdom split apart; the old capital was torn to pieces; Guan Yu obstructed with arms, and the enterprise arose in Eastern Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland fractured and the old capital lay in shards; rebellion blocked the way, and the enterprise of Eastern Jin arose.

sentences.zh: 二庾藉元舅之盛，自許專征，元規臨邾城以覆師，稚恭至襄陽而反旆。

translations.literal: The two Yuans relied on the power of maternal uncles and claimed sole command; Yuan Gui at Zhucheng overturned the army, and Zhigong at Xiangyang turned his banners back.
translations.idiomatic: The two Yuans, leaning on their status as imperial uncles, claimed independent command; Yuan Gui lost his army at Zhucheng, and Zhigong withdrew at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 褚裒以徐、兖勁卒，壹沒於鄒、魯。

translations.literal: Chu Ai with the crack troops of Xu and Yan perished entirely at Zou and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Ai and the elite of Xu and Yan were wiped out at Zou and Lu.

sentences.zh: 殷浩驅楊、豫之眾，大敗於山桑。

translations.literal: Yin Hao drove the hosts of Yang and Yu and was utterly defeated at Shansang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao led the armies of Yang and Yu to crushing defeat at Shansang.

sentences.zh: 桓溫弱冠雄姿，因平蜀之聲勢，步入咸關，野戰洛、鄴。

translations.literal: Huan Wen in his prime had heroic bearing; riding the momentum of pacifying Shu, he marched into Xian Pass and fought in the field at Luo and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, heroic in youth, used the prestige of conquering Shu to march to Xian Pass and fight at Luoyang and Ye.

sentences.zh: 既而鮮卑固於負海，羌、虜割有秦、代，自為敵國，情險勢分，宋武乘機，故能以次而行誅滅。

translations.literal: Then the Xianbei held firm beyond the sea, Qiang and barbarians held Qin and Dai each as enemy states; with perilous sentiments and divided power, Emperor Wu of Song seized the opportunity and so was able to destroy them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Xianbei held the coast, while Qiang and Di held Qin and Dai as rival states; when peril and division opened a path, Emperor Wu of Song seized the moment and destroyed them one by one.

sentences.zh: 及魏虜兼并，河南失境，兵馬土地，非復曩時。

translations.literal: When the Wei barbarians merged and annexed, the south of the Yellow River was lost; troops, horses, and land were no longer as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Northern Wei united the north, the lands south of the Yellow River were lost, and armies, horses, and territory were never again what they had been.

sentences.zh: 宋文雖得之知己，未能料敵，故師帥無功，每戰必殆。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song, though he gained a knowing minister, could not gauge the enemy; hence his commanders achieved no merit and every battle brought peril.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song gained able advisers yet could not read the enemy; his generals won nothing, and every battle brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 泰始以邊臣外叛，遂亡淮北，經略不振，乃議和親。

translations.literal: From Taishi onward, frontier ministers rebelled abroad and Huai-north was lost; strategy languished, and marriage alliance was debated.
translations.idiomatic: From Taishi on, border commanders rebelled and Huai-north was lost; with strategy in decline, the court turned to marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 太祖創命，未及圖遠，戎塵先起，侵暴方牧，淮、豫剋捷，青、海摧奔，以逸待勞，坐微百勝。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor founded the mandate but had not yet planned far; the dust of war rose first, invading border provinces; Huai and Yu were taken in victory, Qing and Hai were shattered in flight—meeting strength with ease, he won a hundred battles while seated.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had barely raised the mandate when war broke out on the frontier; Huai and Yu were won, Qing and Hai swept clean—the court met force with ease and won a hundred victories without stirring.

sentences.zh: 自四州淪沒，民戀本朝，國祚惟新，歌奉威德，提戈荷甲，人自為鬪，深壘結防，想望南旗。

translations.literal: After the four provinces fell, the people yearned for this dynasty; with the state anew, they sang of awesome virtue, bearing spears and armor, each man fighting for himself; deep ramparts and linked defenses looked to the southern banners.
translations.idiomatic: After four provinces were lost, the people still clung to the dynasty; when the state was renewed they praised its power, took up arms of their own will, and behind deep walls watched for the southern banners.

sentences.zh: 天子習知邊事，取亂而授兵律，若前師指日，遠掃臨、彭，而督將逗留，援接稽

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, versed in frontier affairs, took disorder and handed down military law; had the former armies marched on a set day and swept far to Lin and Peng, but the supervising generals lingered and relief came slow
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, skilled in frontier war, took advantage of disorder to issue military law; had the earlier hosts marched on schedule to sweep Lin and Peng, but commanders delayed and reinforcements came too

translations.literal: (dawn)
translations.idiomatic: dawn

sentences.zh: 〔晚〕，向義之徒，傾巢盡室。

translations.literal: [late], those who turned to righteousness emptied nest and household.
translations.idiomatic: late, those who had turned to the cause would have poured out family and home.

sentences.zh: 既失事機，朝議北寢，偃武脩文，更思後會。

translations.literal: The opportunity was lost; court opinion favored resting the northern campaign, sheathing arms and cultivating letters, thinking again of a later meeting.
translations.idiomatic: The moment was lost; the court chose to let the northern campaign sleep, sheathe swords and cultivate learning, and wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 永明之世，據已成之策，職問往來，關禁寧靜。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era they relied on policies already formed; envoys came and went, and the passes were quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongming the court rested on settled policy; envoys passed back and forth and the frontier stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 壃埸之民，竝安堵而息窺覦，百姓附農桑而不失業者，亦由此而已也。

translations.literal: People along the border all dwelled in peace without coveting; common folk kept to farming and sericulture without losing their occupations—this too was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Border folk lived at peace without intrigue; farmers kept to their fields and silkworms—this was part of the reason.

sentences.zh: 夫荊棘所生，用武之弊，寇戎一犯，傷痍難復，豈非此之驗乎？

translations.literal: Where thorns grow, the harm of using arms; once the raiders strike, wounds are hard to heal—is this not proof?
translations.idiomatic: Thorns grow where armies pass; once invaders strike, wounds heal slowly—is this not proof?

sentences.zh: 建武初運，獯雄南逼，豫、徐彊鎮，嬰高城，蓄士卒，不敢與之校武。

translations.literal: At the opening of Jianwu, the Xiongnu pressed south; the strong garrisons of Yu and Xu held high walls, gathered soldiers, and dared not contest in arms.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianwu the Xiongnu pressed south; the great fortresses of Yu and Xu manned their walls and dared not meet the enemy in battle.

sentences.zh: 胡馬蹈藉淮、肥，而常自戰其地。

translations.literal: Hu horses trampled Huai and Fei, yet they constantly fought on that very ground.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses overran the Huai and Fei, yet they fought again and again on the same ground.

sentences.zh: 梯衝之害，鼓掠所亡，建元以來，未之前有。

translations.literal: The harm of scaling ladders and battering rams, what drums and plunder took away—since Jianyuan there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: The ruin of siege ladders and battering rams, the loss to raid and drum—nothing like it had been seen since Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 兼以穹廬華徙，即禮舊都，雍、司北部，親近許、洛，平塗數百，通驛車軌，漢世馳道，直抵章陵，鑣案所騖，晨往暮返。

translations.literal: Moreover the felt tents moved to splendor, taking the old capital as ritual center; northern Yong and Si drew near to Xu and Luo; level roads for hundreds of li, post stations and cart tracks—the Han imperial road ran straight to Zhangling; where the whip rested, one went out at dawn and returned at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The nomad court moved to grandeur and made the old capital its ritual center; northern Yong and Si lay close to Xu and Luo; level roads for hundreds of li bore post-horses and wheel tracks—the Han imperial way ran to Zhangling; where the whip pointed, one could leave at dawn and return by dusk.

sentences.zh: 虜懷兼弱之威，挾廣地之計，彊兵大眾，親自凌殄，旍鼓彌年，矢石不息。

translations.literal: The barbarians held the prestige of combined weakness, the plan of vast territory, strong armies and great hosts personally to crush and destroy; banners and drums for years, arrows and stones without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei wielded the power of a united north and the strategy of wide lands; with vast armies the emperor himself came to crush the south; banners and drums sounded for years, arrows and stones without end.

sentences.zh: 朝規懦屈，莫能救禦，故南陽覆壘，新野頹隍，民戶墾田，皆為狄保。

translations.literal: Court policy was timid and bent; none could rescue or defend; hence Nanyang's ramparts were overturned and Xinye's walls fell; farming households became Di forts.
translations.idiomatic: The court policy was timid and none could save the frontier; Nanyang's walls fell and Xinye collapsed; farmers' fields became barbarian strongholds.

sentences.zh: 雖分遣將卒，俱出淮南，未解沔北之危，已深渦陽之敗。

translations.literal: Though generals were sent separately, all issuing to Huainan, the peril north of the Mian was not relieved before the disaster at Woyang was deep.
translations.idiomatic: Though troops were sent to Huainan, the crisis north of the Mian was not eased before defeat at Woyang deepened the wound.

sentences.zh: 征賦內盡，民命外殫，比屋騷然，不聊生矣。

translations.literal: Tax levies drained the interior and the people's lives were spent abroad; household after household was in turmoil, with no way to live.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes drained the interior and lives were spent on the frontier; household after household knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 夫休𠘶之數，誠有天機，得失之迹，各歸人事。

translations.literal: The measure of rest and toil indeed has heaven's mechanism; the traces of gain and loss each return to human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The rhythm of rest and exertion has its heavenly pattern; the record of gain and loss belongs to human choice.

sentences.zh: 豈不由將率相臨，貪功昧賞，勝敗之急，不相救讓？

translations.literal: Is it not because generals faced one another, greedy for merit and blind to reward, urgent over victory and defeat, and unwilling to rescue or yield?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not because commanders faced one another, greedy for merit and blind to reward, desperate over victory and defeat, and unwilling to aid or yield?

sentences.zh: 號令不明，固中國之所短也。

translations.literal: Unclear orders—this indeed is China's shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Unclear orders—this was truly China's weakness.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天立勍胡，竊有帝圖。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Heaven established the fierce Hu, who stole the imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Heaven raised the fierce Hu, who seized the imperial design.

sentences.zh: 即安諸夏，建號稱孤。

translations.literal: They settled among the Hua, established titles and called themselves sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: They settled among the Chinese, took reign titles, and styled themselves rulers.

sentences.zh: 齊民急病，并邑焚刳。

translations.literal: The people of Qi were pressed by calamity; towns and hamlets were burned and carved.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi suffered pressing calamity; towns and hamlets were burned and gutted.
